{
  "file_path": "/Users/jeevanpillay/Code/@lightfastai/lightfast/.agents/skills/lightfast-clerk/lib/common.sh",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Shared helpers for lightfast-clerk skill.\n#\n# All scripts source this. Contains:\n#  - Safety guardrails (pk_test-only, localhost-only by default)\n#  - Profile path resolution (per-repo under .agent-browser/)\n#  - Default email derivation from git config\n#  - Meta sidecar helpers (load/save user+org ids)\n#\n# Scripts should `set -euo pipefail` and then `source lib/common.sh`.\n\n# Resolve repo root from the skill location (three levels up: lib/ -> skill/ -> skills/ -> .agents/)\nLIGHTFAST_CLERK_REPO_ROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/../../../..\" && pwd)\"\nexport LIGHTFAST_CLERK_REPO_ROOT\n\nLIGHTFAST_CLERK_PROFILES_DIR=\"${LIGHTFAST_CLERK_REPO_ROOT}/.agent-browser/profiles\"\nexport LIGHTFAST_CLERK_PROFILES_DIR\n\n# Default base URL. Override with LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL.\nLIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL=\"${LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL:-http://localhost:3024}\"\nexport LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL\n\n# --- logging ---------------------------------------------------------------\n\nlog()  { printf '[lightfast-clerk] %s\\n' \"$*\" >&2; }\nerr()  { printf '[lightfast-clerk] ERROR: %s\\n' \"$*\" >&2; }\ndie()  { err \"$*\"; exit 1; }\n\n# --- safety ----------------------------------------------------------------\n\n# Refuse if the configured Clerk publishable key is a live key.\n# Refuse if target URL is not localhost unless explicitly overridden.\nassert_safe_env() {\n  local env_file=\"${LIGHTFAST_CLERK_REPO_ROOT}/apps/app/.vercel/.env.development.local\"\n  if [[ ! -f \"$env_file\" ]]; then\n    die \"missing env file: $env_file  (run 'vercel env pull' in apps/app?)\"\n  fi\n\n  # Grep the publishable key line; strip quotes; first 8 chars must be pk_test_.\n  local pk\n  pk=\"$(grep -E '^NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=' \"$env_file\" | head -n1 \\\n        | sed -E 's/^[^=]+=//; s/^\"//; s/\"$//')\"\n  if [[ -z \"$pk\" ]]; then\n    die \"NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY not found in $env_file\"\n  fi\n  if [[ \"$pk\" != pk_test_* ]]; then\n    die \"refusing to run against non-test Clerk key (starts with '${pk:0:8}'). This skill is dev-only.\"\n  fi\n\n  # URL guardrail\n  if [[ \"${LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL}\" != http://localhost:* && \"${LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL}\" != http://127.0.0.1:* ]]; then\n    if [[ \"${LIGHTFAST_CLERK_I_KNOW_WHAT_IM_DOING:-0}\" != \"1\" ]]; then\n      die \"LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL='${LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL}' is not localhost. Set LIGHTFAST_CLERK_I_KNOW_WHAT_IM_DOING=1 to override.\"\n    fi\n  fi\n}\n\n# Reject profile names that would escape the profiles dir or overwrite siblings.\nassert_profile_name() {\n  local name=\"$1\"\n  [[ -n \"$name\" ]] || die \"profile name is required\"\n  [[ \"$name\" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ ]] || die \"profile name must match [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+; got: $name\"\n}\n\nprofile_dir() {\n  local name=\"$1\"\n  assert_profile_name \"$name\"\n  printf '%s/%s' \"$LIGHTFAST_CLERK_PROFILES_DIR\" \"$name\"\n}\n\nprofile_meta_path() {\n  local name=\"$1\"\n  assert_profile_name \"$name\"\n  printf '%s/%s.meta.json' \"$LIGHTFAST_CLERK_PROFILES_DIR\" \"$name\"\n}\n\n# --- email derivation ------------------------------------------------------\n\n# Derive a test email from git config. Example:\n#   git user.email = \"jp@jeevanpillay.com\"\n#   → \"debug-jp-jeevanpillay-com+clerk_test@lightfast.ai\"\n#\n# Clerk test mode delivers nothing but requires \"+clerk_test\" suffix in the\n# local-part. Using lightfast.ai as the domain keeps stray emails off the\n# developer's personal inbox if test mode is ever bypassed.\nderive_test_email() {\n  local git_email\n  git_email=\"$(git -C \"$LIGHTFAST_CLERK_REPO_ROOT\" config user.email 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n  [[ -n \"$git_email\" ]] || die \"git user.email not set. Set it or pass an email explicitly.\"\n\n  local slug\n  slug=\"$(printf '%s' \"$git_email\" \\\n    | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' \\\n    | sed -E 's/@/-/g; s/\\./-/g; s/[^a-z0-9-]/-/g; s/-+/-/g; s/^-+//; s/-+$//')\"\n  [[ -n \"$slug\" ]] || die \"could not derive slug from git email: $git_email\"\n\n  printf 'debug-%s+clerk_test@lightfast.ai' \"$slug\"\n}\n\n# --- meta sidecar ----------------------------------------------------------\n\n# Write/merge fields into <profile>.meta.json. Uses node for safe JSON merging\n# (jq isn't guaranteed installed on dev boxes). Keys that are null are deleted.\n# Usage: meta_write <profile> <json-object>\nmeta_write() {\n  local profile=\"$1\"\n  local patch=\"$2\"\n  local path\n  path=\"$(profile_meta_path \"$profile\")\"\n  mkdir -p \"$(dirname \"$path\")\"\n  node --input-type=module -e \"\n    import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs';\n    const path = '${path}';\n    const patch = ${patch};\n    const current = existsSync(path) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')) : {};\n    const next = { ...current, ...patch };\n    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(patch)) if (v === null) delete next[k];\n    writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(next, null, 2) + '\\n');\n  \"\n}\n\nmeta_read() {\n  local profile=\"$1\"\n  local key=\"$2\"\n  local path\n  path=\"$(profile_meta_path \"$profile\")\"\n  [[ -f \"$path\" ]] || { printf ''; return 0; }\n  node --input-type=module -e \"\n    import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\n    const m = JSON.parse(readFileSync('${path}', 'utf8'));\n    const v = m['${key}'];\n    if (v !== undefined && v !== null) process.stdout.write(String(v));\n  \"\n}\n\n# --- agent-browser wrapper -------------------------------------------------\n\n# Run agent-browser bound to a profile, with consistent flags.\n# Usage: ab <profile> <args...>\nab() {\n  local profile=\"$1\"; shift\n  local dir\n  dir=\"$(profile_dir \"$profile\")\"\n  mkdir -p \"$dir\"\n  agent-browser --profile \"$dir\" --session \"lightfast-clerk-$profile\" \"$@\"\n}\n"
}

export function CodeVerificationUI({

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Sign in a Clerk test user via email + OTP 424242. Idempotent.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   login.sh <profile> [email]\n#\n# Profile is a short name (a-z0-9_-). Poll up to 10s.\nfor _ in $(seq 1 20); do\n  loaded=$(ab \"$PROFILE\" eval \"typeof window.Clerk !== 'undefined' && window.Clerk.loaded\" 2>/dev/null || printf 'false')\n  [[ \"$loaded\" == \"true\" ]] && break\n  sleep 0.5\ndone\n\nexisting_user=$(ab \"$PROFILE\" eval \"window.Clerk?.user?.id ?? null\" 2>/dev/null || printf 'null')\nif [[ \"$existing_user\" != \"null\" && -n \"$existing_user\" ]]; then\n  log \"already signed in as user=$existing_user — refreshing meta\"\n  meta_write \"$PROFILE\" \"{ email: '$EMAIL', userId: '$existing_user', signedInAt: new Date().toISOString() }\"\n  ab \"$PROFILE\" close >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n  log \"OK\"\n  exit 0\nfi\n\n# --- Sign-in flow -----------------------------------------------------------\n\nlog \"navigating to /sign-in\"\nab \"$PROFILE\" open \"$LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL/sign-in\" >/dev/null\n\nlog \"waiting for email input\"\nab \"$PROFILE\" wait 'input[name=email]' >/dev/null\n\nlog \"submitting email\"\nab \"$PROFILE\" fill 'input[name=email]' \"$EMAIL\" >/dev/null\n# The \"Continue with Email\" submit button is the only button on this form.\nab \"$PROFILE\" find role button \"Continue with Email\" click >/dev/null\n\nlog \"waiting for OTP input\"\n# shadcn InputOTP renders a hidden input with data-input-otp. Wait for it.\nfor _ in $(seq 1 20); do\n  ready=$(ab \"$PROFILE\" eval \"!!document.querySelector('input[data-input-otp]')\" 2>/dev/null || printf 'false')\n  [[ \"$ready\" == \"true\" ]] && break\n  sleep 0.5\ndone\n[[ \"$ready\" == \"true\" ]] || die \"OTP input did not appear within 10s\"\n\nlog \"typing OTP 424242\"\nab \"$PROFILE\" focus 'input[data-input-otp]' >/dev/null\nab \"$PROFILE\" keyboard type '424242' >/dev/null\n\nlog \"waiting for sign-in to complete (redirect away from /sign-in)\"\nfor _ in $(seq 1 30); do\n  url=$(ab \"$PROFILE\" get url 2>/dev/null || printf '')\n  [[ \"$url\" != *\"/sign-in\"* && -n \"$url\" ]] && break\n  sleep 1\ndone\n[[ \"$url\" != *\"/sign-in\"* ]] || die \"still on /sign-in after 30s — verification likely failed (current url: $url)\"\nlog \"redirected to: $url\"\n\n# Wait for Clerk client to settle on the new page\nfor _ in $(seq 1 20); do\n  loaded=$(ab \"$PROFILE\" eval \"typeof window.Clerk !== 'undefined' && window.Clerk.loaded && !!window.Clerk.user\" 2>/dev/null || printf 'false')\n  [[ \"$loaded\" == \"true\" ]] && break\n  sleep 0.5\ndone\n\nUSER_ID=$(ab \"$PROFILE\" eval \"window.Clerk?.user?.id\" 2>/dev/null || printf '')\n[[ -n \"$USER_ID\" && \"$USER_ID\" != \"null\" ]] || die \"could not read Clerk user id after sign-in\"\n\nmeta_write \"$PROFILE\" \"{ email: '$EMAIL', userId: '$USER_ID', signedInAt: new Date().toISOString() }\"\nab \"$PROFILE\" close >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n\nlog \"OK — signed in as user=$USER_ID\"\n"

"use client";

import { toast } from "@repo/ui/components/ui/sonner";
import { addBreadcrumb, startSpan } from "@sentry/nextjs";
import { useSignIn, useSignUp } from "@vendor/clerk/client";
import * as React from "react";
import { CodeVerificationUI } from "./shared/code-verification-ui";

interface OTPIslandProps {
  email: string | null;
  mode: "sign-in" | "sign-up";
  onError?: (message: string, isWaitlist?: boolean) => void;
  ticket?: string | null;
}

export function OTPIsland({ email, mode, ticket, onError }: OTPIslandProps) {
  const { signIn } = useSignIn();
  const { signUp } = useSignUp();

  const [code, setCode] = React.useState("");
  const [error, setError] = React.useState<string | null>(null);
  const [isVerifying, setIsVerifying] = React.useState(false);
  const [isRedirecting, setIsRedirecting] = React.useState(false);
  const [isResending, setIsResending] = React.useState(false);
  const [isInitializing, setIsInitializing] = React.useState(true);
  // Tracks the display email — seeded from prop, populated from Clerk on ticket-only path
  const [resolvedEmail, setResolvedEmail] = React.useState<string | null>(
    email
  );

  const navigateToConsole = React.useCallback(() => {
    window.location.href = "/account/welcome";
  }, []);

  const handleClerkError = React.useCallback(
    (
      clerkError: {
        code: string;
        message?: string;
        longMessage?: string;
      } | null
    ) => {
      if (!clerkError) {
        return;
      }
      const errCode = clerkError.code;

      if (errCode === "too_many_requests") {
        setError("Too many attempts. Please wait a moment and try again.");
        return;
      }
      if (errCode === "user_locked") {
        setError("Account locked. Please try again later.");
        return;
      }
      if (errCode === "sign_up_restricted_waitlist") {
        const msg =
          "Sign-ups are currently unavailable. Join the waitlist to be notified when access becomes available.";
        if (onError) {
          onError(msg, true);
        } else {
          window.location.href = `/sign-up?error=${encodeURIComponent(msg)}&waitlist=true`;
        }
        return;
      }
      setError(
        clerkError.longMessage ?? clerkError.message ?? "Verification failed"
      );
    },
    [onError]
  );

  const hasInitRef = React.useRef(false);
  const verifyingCodeRef = React.useRef<string | null>(null);

  // Send OTP on mount (or handle ticket)
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (hasInitRef.current) {
      return;
    }
    hasInitRef.current = true;

    async function init() {
      if (mode === "sign-up" && ticket) {
        // Invitation ticket flow: create sign-up with ticket + email + legal in one call.
        // ticket bypasses waitlist; emailAddress is whatever the user wants (not required to
        // match the invited address); legalAccepted satisfies the legal_accepted requirement.
        const { error: createError } = await signUp.create({
          ticket,
          emailAddress: email ?? undefined,
          legalAccepted: true,
        });

"use server";

import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
import { z } from "zod";
import { serializeSignUpParams } from "../_lib/search-params";

const emailSchema = z.object({
  email: z.string().email("Please enter a valid email address"),
  ticket: z.string().optional(),
});

export async function initiateSignUp(formData: FormData) {
  const parsed = emailSchema.safeParse({
    email: formData.get("email"),
    ticket: formData.get("ticket") || undefined,
  });

  if (!parsed.success) {
    const message =
      parsed.error.flatten().fieldErrors.email?.[0] ?? "Invalid email";
    const rawTicket = (formData.get("ticket") as string | null) ?? undefined;
    redirect(
      serializeSignUpParams("/sign-up", {
        error: message,
        ticket: rawTicket ?? null,
      })
    );
  }

  // Email validated. Redirect to OTP step — the client island will handle
  // signUp.emailCode.sendCode() or signUp.ticket() via Clerk's FAPI.
  redirect(
    serializeSignUpParams("/sign-up", {
      step: "code",
      email: parsed.data.email,
      ticket: parsed.data.ticket ?? null,
    })
  );
}

function decodeTicketExpiry(ticket: string): Date | null {
  try {
    const segment = ticket.split(".")[1];
    if (!segment) {
      return null;
    }
    const payload = JSON.parse(
      atob(segment.replace(/-/g, "+").replace(/_/g, "/"))
    ) as { exp?: unknown };
    return typeof payload.exp === "number"
      ? new Date(payload.exp * 1000)
      : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

Dev-only.`\n  );\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n\nasync function clerk(method, path, body) {\n  const res = await fetch(`${CLERK_API}${path}`, {\n    method,\n    headers: {\n      authorization: `Bearer ${SECRET}`,\n      \"content-type\": \"application/json\",\n    },\n    body: body !== undefined ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,\n  });\n  const text = await res.text();\n  let json = null;\n  try { json = text ? JSON.parse(text) : null; } catch {}\n  if (!res.ok) {\n    const detail = json?.errors?.[0]?.long_message ?? json?.errors?.[0]?.message ?? text;\n    throw new Error(`Clerk ${method} ${path} → ${res.status}: ${detail}`);\n  }\n  return json;\n}\n\nasync function findUserByEmail(email) {\n  // Clerk's filter uses `email_address` (repeatable, comma-separated)\n  const params = new URLSearchParams({ email_address: email, limit: \"1\" });\n  const list = await clerk(\"GET\", `/users?${params}`);\n  return Array.isArray(list) && list.length > 0 ? list[0] : null;\n}\n\nasync function ensureUser(email) {\n  const existing = await findUserByEmail(email);\n  if (existing) return existing.id;\n  const created = await clerk(\"POST\", \"/users\", {\n    email_address: [email],\n    skip_password_requirement: true,\n  });\n  return created.id;\n}\n\nasync function deleteUser(userId) {\n  await clerk(\"DELETE\", `/users/${userId}`);\n}\n\nasync function mintSessionToken(userId, template) {\n  // Create a session for the user\n  const session = await clerk(\"POST\", \"/sessions\", { user_id: userId });\n  // Mint a token. With template path, /tokens/{template}; default template is /tokens\n  const path = template\n    ? `/sessions/${session.id}/tokens/${encodeURIComponent(template)}`\n    : `/sessions/${session.id}/tokens`;\n  const res = await clerk(\"POST\", path, {});\n  return res.jwt;\n}\n\nconst [, , subcommand, ...args] = process.argv;\n\ntry {\n  switch (subcommand) {\n    case \"ensure-user\": {\n      const [email] = args;\n      if (!email) throw new Error(\"ensure-user requires <email>\");\n      const id = await ensureUser(email);\n      process.stdout.write(id);\n      break;\n    }\n    case \"delete-user\": {\n      const [userId] = args;\n      if (!userId) throw new Error(\"delete-user requires <userId>\");\n      await deleteUser(userId);\n      break;\n    }\n    case \"mint-session-token\": {\n      const [userId, template] = args;\n      if (!userId) throw new Error(\"mint-session-token requires <userId> [template]\");\n      const jwt = await mintSessionToken(userId, template);\n      process.stdout.write(jwt);\n      break;\n    }\n    default:\n      console.error(`unknown subcommand: ${subcommand}`);\n      console.error(`usage: ${process.argv[1]} <ensure-user|delete-user|mint-session-token> ...`);\n      process.exit(2);\n  }\n} catch (err) {\n  console.error(`[clerk-backend] ${err.message}`);\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n"

> AGENT

**Phase 1 green path confirmed**: `200` with full profile JSON via mesh (3024) + valid Bearer. `resolveClerkSession` works end-to-end against real Clerk. Two findings worth noting:

- **Clerk middleware passes Bearer tokens through** — no `proxy.ts` change needed for the happy path.
- **Garbage Bearer → 500** (not 401). Middleware tries to verify, throws on malformed JWT. Phase 5's renderer 401 handler will need to treat 500 as "re-auth" or we'll need to add `/api/trpc/(.*)` to `isApiRoute`. Not a Phase 1 blocker.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/jeevanpillay/Code/@lightfastai/lightfast/.agents/skills/lightfast-clerk/command/token.sh",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Mint a Clerk session JWT for a profile. Backend-only — no browser needed.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   token.sh <profile> [template]\n#\n# Stdout: a single JWT line (no decoration). Stderr: progress + errors.\n# Exit codes:\n#   0  ok\n#   1  unexpected error\n#   2  no user yet — run login.sh <profile> first (or set LIGHTFAST_CLERK_EMAIL\n#      and we'll provision the user inline)\n#\n# Why backend instead of browser eval:\n#   - Faster (no browser process, no page load)\n#   - Reliable (no React-state timing)\n#   - Works for arbitrary JWT templates (browser eval depends on Clerk JS state)\n# Browser sign-in via login.sh is still required if you need a persisted Clerk\n# cookie for desktop renderer / BrowserWindow flows.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\n# shellcheck source=../lib/common.sh\nsource \"$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/common.sh\"\n\nPROFILE=\"${1:-}\"\nTEMPLATE=\"${2:-}\"\n[[ -n \"$PROFILE\" ]] || die \"usage: token.sh <profile> [template]\"\n\nassert_safe_env\nassert_profile_name \"$PROFILE\"\n\nUSER_ID=\"$(meta_read \"$PROFILE\" userId)\"\n\nif [[ -z \"$USER_ID\" ]]; then\n  # No meta sidecar yet — provision the user inline so token.sh works\n  # standalone. Email derives from git config (or LIGHTFAST_CLERK_EMAIL).\n  EMAIL=\"${LIGHTFAST_CLERK_EMAIL:-$(derive_test_email)}\"\n  log \"no profile meta found — provisioning user for $EMAIL\"\n  USER_ID=$(node \"$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/clerk-backend.mjs\" ensure-user \"$EMAIL\")\n  [[ -n \"$USER_ID\" ]] || die \"ensure-user returned empty id\"\n  meta_write \"$PROFILE\" \"{ email: '$EMAIL', userId: '$USER_ID', signedInAt: new Date().toISOString() }\"\n  log \"provisioned user=$USER_ID (note: no browser session — run login.sh if you need cookie persistence)\"\nfi\n\nlog \"minting token for user=$USER_ID${TEMPLATE:+ template=$TEMPLATE}\"\nnode \"$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/clerk-backend.mjs\" mint-session-token \"$USER_ID\" \"$TEMPLATE\"\n# trailing newline so consumers using $(token.sh) don't end up with weird trailing content\nprintf '\\n'\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/jeevanpillay/Code/@lightfastai/lightfast/.agents/skills/lightfast-clerk/command/status.sh",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Report the state of a lightfast-clerk profile.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   status.sh <profile>\n#\n# Prints one of (human-readable to stdout; machine-parseable with --json):\n#   UNKNOWN              no meta sidecar, no profile dir\n#   PROVISIONED          user exists in Clerk, no browser session\n#   SIGNED_IN            user exists AND browser profile has a live Clerk session\n#   SIGNED_OUT           profile exists but session was cleared\n#\n# Exit: 0 on any known state, 1 on error.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\n# shellcheck source=../lib/common.sh\nsource \"$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/common.sh\"\n\nPROFILE=\"${1:-}\"\n[[ -n \"$PROFILE\" ]] || die \"usage: status.sh <profile>\"\nassert_profile_name \"$PROFILE\"\n\nMETA_PATH=\"$(profile_meta_path \"$PROFILE\")\"\nPROF_PATH=\"$(profile_dir \"$PROFILE\")\"\nUSER_ID=\"$(meta_read \"$PROFILE\" userId)\"\nEMAIL=\"$(meta_read \"$PROFILE\" email)\"\n\n# 1) No meta and no profile dir → UNKNOWN\nif [[ -z \"$USER_ID\" && ! -d \"$PROF_PATH\" ]]; then\n  printf 'state: UNKNOWN (profile=%s)\\n' \"$PROFILE\"\n  exit 0\nfi\n\n# 2) Only meta (provisioned, never browser-signed-in) → PROVISIONED\nif [[ -n \"$USER_ID\" && ! -d \"$PROF_PATH\" ]]; then\n  printf 'state: PROVISIONED\\n  profile: %s\\n  email: %s\\n  userId: %s\\n' \\\n    \"$PROFILE\" \"$EMAIL\" \"$USER_ID\"\n  exit 0\nfi\n\n# 3) Has profile dir — probe browser for live session.\n#    This is the slow path (~2-3s) because it spins up a browser.\nassert_safe_env\nab \"$PROFILE\" open \"$LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL/sign-in\" >/dev/null\nsleep 1\nlanding_url=\"$(ab_eval_raw \"$PROFILE\" \"location.href\")\"\nab \"$PROFILE\" close >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n\nif [[ \"$landing_url\" == *\"/sign-in\"* || -z \"$landing_url\" ]]; then\n  state=\"SIGNED_OUT\"\nelse\n  state=\"SIGNED_IN\"\nfi\n\nprintf 'state: %s\\n  profile: %s\\n  email: %s\\n  userId: %s\\n  landingUrl: %s\\n' \\\n  \"$state\" \"$PROFILE\" \"$EMAIL\" \"$USER_ID\" \"$landing_url\"\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/jeevanpillay/Code/@lightfastai/lightfast/.agents/skills/lightfast-clerk/command/signout.sh",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Sign out the current Clerk session for a profile (server-side invalidate).\n# Profile dir + meta sidecar are kept — re-login is fast (cookies still cached).\n# For a full disk-level wipe, use reset.sh.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   signout.sh <profile>\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\n# shellcheck source=../lib/common.sh\nsource \"$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/common.sh\"\n\nPROFILE=\"${1:-}\"\n[[ -n \"$PROFILE\" ]] || die \"usage: signout.sh <profile>\"\n\nassert_safe_env\nassert_profile_name \"$PROFILE\"\n\nPROF_PATH=\"$(profile_dir \"$PROFILE\")\"\nif [[ ! -d \"$PROF_PATH\" ]]; then\n  log \"no profile dir for '$PROFILE' — nothing to sign out\"\n  exit 0\nfi\n\n# Open any authed page so window.Clerk loads. /sign-in redirects to\n# /account/welcome when signed in, which exposes Clerk client.\nab \"$PROFILE\" open \"$LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL/sign-in\" >/dev/null\nsleep 1\n\n# If we landed back on /sign-in, we were already signed out.\nurl=$(ab_eval_raw \"$PROFILE\" \"location.href\")\nif [[ \"$url\" == *\"/sign-in\"* ]]; then\n  log \"already signed out (landed on $url)\"\n  ab \"$PROFILE\" close >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nlog \"calling Clerk.signOut()\"\nab \"$PROFILE\" eval \"await window.Clerk.signOut()\" >/dev/null\n\n# Verify\nsleep 1\nab \"$PROFILE\" open \"$LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL/sign-in\" >/dev/null\nsleep 1\nfinal_url=$(ab_eval_raw \"$PROFILE\" \"location.href\")\nab \"$PROFILE\" close >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n\nif [[ \"$final_url\" == *\"/sign-in\"* ]]; then\n  log \"OK — signed out (now lands on $final_url)\"\nelse\n  die \"signout reported success but still landing on $final_url\"\nfi\n"
}

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Convenience wrapper: mint a JWT and curl a tRPC procedure.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   curl.sh <profile> <procedure> [json-body]            # GET if no body\n#   curl.sh <profile> <procedure> '{\"foo\":\"bar\"}'        # POST with JSON body\n#   curl.sh -t <template> <profile> <procedure> [body]   # use a JWT template\n#   curl.sh --raw <profile> <procedure> [body]           # skip tRPC batching\n#\n# By default, GET calls are wrapped in tRPC's batch=1 envelope:\n#   /api/trpc/<procedure>?batch=1&input={\"0\":{\"json\":<body|null>}}\n# Use --raw if you're calling a procedure that doesn't use batching.\n#\n# Output: response body to stdout, status to stderr.\n# Exit: curl's exit code (0 on 2xx, non-zero otherwise — checked via http_code).\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\n# shellcheck source=../lib/common.sh\nsource \"$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/common.sh\"\n\nTEMPLATE=\"\"\nRAW=0\n\n# Parse leading flags\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n  case \"$1\" in\n    -t|--template) TEMPLATE=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n    --raw) RAW=1; shift ;;\n    -h|--help)\n      sed -nE '/^# /,/^[^#]/p' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n      exit 0\n      ;;\n    --) shift; break ;;\n    -*) die \"unknown option: $1\" ;;\n    *) break ;;\n  esac\ndone\n\nPROFILE=\"${1:-}\"; shift || true\nPROCEDURE=\"${1:-}\"; shift || true\nBODY=\"${1:-}\"\n[[ -n \"$PROFILE\" && -n \"$PROCEDURE\" ]] || die \"usage: curl.sh [-t template] [--raw] <profile> <procedure> [json-body]\"\n\nassert_safe_env\n\n# Mint the JWT (token.sh writes log to stderr; we only capture stdout)\nTOKEN=\"$(\"$SCRIPT_DIR/token.sh\" \"$PROFILE\" \"$TEMPLATE\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\n')\"\n[[ -n \"$TOKEN\" ]] || die \"token.sh returned empty token (run login.sh $PROFILE first?)\"\n\nURL=\"$LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL/api/trpc/$PROCEDURE\"\nif [[ \"$RAW\" == \"0\" ]]; then\n  # Wrap body in tRPC batch envelope\n  if [[ -n \"$BODY\" ]]; then\n    INPUT=\"{\\\"0\\\":{\\\"json\\\":$BODY}}\"\n  else\n    INPUT='{\"0\":{\"json\":null}}'\n  fi\n  ENCODED_INPUT=$(node -e \"process.stdout.write(encodeURIComponent(process.argv[1]))\" \"$INPUT\")\n  URL=\"${URL}?batch=1&input=${ENCODED_INPUT}\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -n \"$BODY\" && \"$RAW\" == \"0\" ]]; then\n  # Batched calls send input via query string for GET-shaped queries; mutations\n  # use POST with the body in the request payload. Default to GET unless body\n  # is set AND the user explicitly wants POST (--raw + body).\n  METHOD=\"GET\"\nelif [[ -n \"$BODY\" ]]; then\n  METHOD=\"POST\"\nelse\n  METHOD=\"GET\"\nfi\n\nlog \"${METHOD} ${URL}  (token: ${TOKEN:0:20}...${TOKEN: -10})\"\n\nif [[ \"$METHOD\" == \"POST\" ]]; then\n  curl -sS -X POST \\\n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\\n    -H \"x-trpc-source: lightfast-clerk-skill\" \\\n    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n    -d \"$BODY\" \\\n    -w \"\\n[HTTP %{http_code}]\\n\" \\\n    \"$URL\"\nelse\n  curl -sS \\\n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\\n    -H \"x-trpc-source: lightfast-clerk-skill\" \\\n    -w \"\\n[HTTP %{http_code}]\\n\" \\\n    \"$URL\"\nfi\n"
}

  "content": "---\nname: lightfast-clerk\ndescription: |\n  Provision Clerk test users, sign in via the browser, mint JWTs, and tear\n  everything down — for local-dev tRPC / desktop / API testing. Triggers when\n  the user wants to call Lightfast tRPC procedures with a real auth token,\n  test desktop sign-in flows, or set up / clean up test users in Clerk dev.\n  Dev-only: refuses to run against pk_live_ keys or non-localhost URLs.\n---\n\n# Lightfast Clerk Skill\n\nEnd-to-end Clerk auth automation for local development. Provisions test users,\ndrives sign-in, mints JWTs, and cleans up — all without human interaction.\n\n## Decision tree\n\n```\nWhat do you need?\n├── A JWT to call /api/trpc/...               -> command/token.sh <profile> [template]\n├── A live browser session (cookie persisted) -> command/login.sh <profile>\n├── Inspect a profile's state                 -> command/status.sh <profile>\n├── Curl a tRPC procedure with auth           -> command/curl.sh <profile> <procedure>\n├── Sign out (server-side, keep profile)      -> command/signout.sh <profile>\n├── Wipe local profile state                  -> command/reset.sh <profile>\n└── Delete the Clerk user entirely            -> command/delete-user.sh <profile>\n```\n\n**Most common workflow** (testing a tRPC procedure):\n```bash\n.agents/skills/lightfast-clerk/command/curl.sh -t lightfast-desktop claude-default account.get\n```\nThis single call handles user provisioning, token minting, and the curl in one step.\n\n## Commands\n\n| Command | Purpose | Browser? | Side effects |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `token.sh <profile> [template]` | Mint a JWT (stdout = JWT) | No | Provisions user if first call |\n| `login.sh <profile> [email]` | Browser sign-in for cookie persistence | Yes (headless) | Provisions user, persists Clerk cookie |\n| `status.sh <profile>` | Report profile state | Yes (headless) | None |\n| `signout.sh <profile>` | Server-side sign out | Yes (headless) | Clerk session invalidated |\n| `reset.sh <profile>` | Wipe profile dir + meta | No | `rm -rf` profile |\n| `delete-user.sh <profile>` | Delete Clerk user + reset | No | Clerk user permanently removed |\n| `curl.sh [-t tpl] <profile> <proc> [body]` | Mint + curl convenience | No | None |\n\n## Mental model\n\nA **profile** = `<repo>/.agent-browser/profiles/<name>/` (Playwright user-data-dir)\n+ `<name>.meta.json` sidecar (`email`, `userId`, `signedInAt`).\n\nProfiles are **per-repo, gitignored**, scoped to one Clerk test user each.\n\nState machine:\n```\n[UNKNOWN]                                              ┌─────────────┐\n   │  token.sh ─ provisions user (Backend API)         │ delete-user │\n   ▼                                                   │   (Clerk)   │\n[PROVISIONED] ──login.sh──> [SIGNED_IN]                │             │\n                                │                      └──────┬──────┘\n                                │ signout.sh                  ▼\n                                ▼                       [UNKNOWN] (no Clerk user, no disk)\n                          [SIGNED_OUT] ──login.sh──┐\n                                │                  │\n                                │ reset.sh         │\n                                ▼                  │\n                          [UNKNOWN]                │\n                                                   │\n                          (re-login) ──────────────┘\n```\n\n## Key conventions\n\n- **Profile name**: `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`. Default profile in examples: `claude-default`.\n- **Email**: derived from `git config user.email`. GitHub noreply → just the username.\n  Example: `jp@jeevanpillay.com` → `debug-jp-jeevanpillay-com+clerk_test@lightfast.ai`.\n  Override with `LIGHTFAST_CLERK_EMAIL=...`.\n- **JWT template**: pass `lightfast-desktop` for desktop-shape JWTs (1h expiry,\n  `org_id` claim). Omit for the default Clerk session token.\n- **Base URL**: `http://localhost:3024` (mesh origin). Override via `LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL`.\n  Non-localhost URLs require `LIGHTFAST_CLERK_I_KNOW_WHAT_IM_DOING=1`.\n\n## Safety guardrails\n\nEvery script aborts immediately if any of these fire:\n1. Clerk publishable key in `apps/app/.vercel/.env.development.local` is not `pk_test_*`\n2. Target URL is not localhost AND override flag is unset\n3. Profile name contains characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]`\n4. Email passed to `login.sh` does not contain `+clerk_test@`\n\nBackend operations (`clerk-backend.mjs`) refuse non-test secret keys.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n1. **Dev server running**: `pnpm dev:app` (or `pnpm dev:desktop-stack` once Phase 6 lands).\n   Skill targets `http://localhost:3024` (microfrontends mesh).\n2. **`agent-browser` CLI installed**: `which agent-browser` should resolve.\n3. **`.vercel/.env.development.local` pulled**: `cd apps/app && vercel env pull`.\n4. **JWT template in Clerk dashboard** (only needed if you want template-shaped tokens):\n   - Name: `lightfast-desktop`\n   - Expiry: 3600s\n   - Claims: `{ \"org_id\": \"{{org.id}}\" }`\n\n## Background — Clerk test mode\n\nThe `pk_test_` / `sk_test_` Clerk keys enable test mode:\n- Emails matching `<anything>+clerk_test@<anydomain>` skip real delivery\n- OTP code `424242` always verifies in those flows\n- Backend-created users skip waitlist gating\n\nThis is what makes the skill fully scriptable. See `references/test-mode.md`.\n\n## See also\n\n- `references/safety.md` — guardrails in detail\n- `references/test-mode.md` — Clerk test-mode primer\n- `references/jwt-templates.md` — template names + claims\n- `lib/common.sh` — shared bash helpers (sourced by all commands)\n- `lib/clerk-backend.mjs` — Backend API wrapper (ensure-user, delete-user, mint-session-token)\n"

  "content": "# Safety guardrails\n\nThis skill performs **side-effecting Clerk operations** (creating users, signing\nin, deleting users). It is **dev-only**. Multiple guardrails enforce this.\n\n## Layered defenses\n\n### 1. Test-key check (`assert_safe_env` in `lib/common.sh`)\n\nReads `apps/app/.vercel/.env.development.local`. Aborts if:\n- File missing\n- `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` missing\n- Key does not start with `pk_test_`\n\nBackend script (`lib/clerk-backend.mjs`) does the same check on `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`\n(must start with `sk_test_`).\n\n### 2. URL allowlist\n\nDefault `LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL=http://localhost:3024`. Non-localhost URLs require:\n```bash\nLIGHTFAST_CLERK_I_KNOW_WHAT_IM_DOING=1\n```\nThis is intentionally awkward to type. There is no production use case for this\nskill; the override exists only for branch-preview testing.\n\n### 3. Profile name lock\n\n`assert_profile_name` rejects anything outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`. Prevents path\ntraversal (`../`) and accidental shell-expansion attacks.\n\n### 4. Profile path scope\n\nAll profiles live under `<repo>/.agent-browser/profiles/`. The path is computed\nfrom the skill's `lib/` location (relative resolution, not configurable). No\nscript accepts an absolute path argument.\n\n### 5. Email allowlist (login.sh only)\n\n`login.sh` refuses any email that does not contain `+clerk_test@`. Prevents\naccidentally driving sign-in for a real Clerk user.\n\nThis guard does **not** apply to `token.sh` if you call it without first running\n`login.sh` — `token.sh` will provision whatever email `derive_test_email` returns\nor `LIGHTFAST_CLERK_EMAIL` is set to. Set responsibly.\n\n### 6. .gitignore\n\n`.agent-browser/` is gitignored. Profile dirs contain Clerk session cookies and\nshould never be committed.\n\n## What's NOT guarded\n\n- The skill cannot detect if a Clerk test instance has been pointed at a\n  production database (would be a misconfiguration upstream).\n- `delete-user.sh` is irreversible — Clerk does not retain deleted user data.\n  No \"are you sure?\" prompt because the skill is for ephemeral test users.\n\n## Failure modes worth knowing\n\n| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| `refusing to run against non-test Clerk key` | Live keys in `.env.development.local` | Restore test keys (`vercel env pull` from dev project) |\n| `LIGHTFAST_CLERK_URL=... is not localhost` | Custom URL without override | Set `LIGHTFAST_CLERK_I_KNOW_WHAT_IM_DOING=1` only if you really mean it |\n| `email '...' is not a Clerk test address` | Custom email lacks `+clerk_test@` | Use the derived format or set `LIGHTFAST_CLERK_EMAIL` to one that includes it |\n| `profile name must match [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+` | Spaces, dots, slashes | Use a simple identifier |\n"

  "content": "# Clerk test mode primer\n\nThis skill relies on Clerk's [test mode](https://clerk.com/docs/testing/test-emails-and-phones)\nto fully automate sign-in. Test mode is enabled implicitly by using `pk_test_` /\n`sk_test_` keys.\n\n## What test mode does\n\n### 1. Test email pattern\n\nEmail addresses matching this regex are treated as test addresses:\n```\n^.+\\+clerk_test@.+$\n```\n\nExamples:\n- `debug-jp+clerk_test@lightfast.ai` ✅\n- `claude+clerk_test@example.com` ✅\n- `jp+clerk_test_v2@anything.com` ❌ (must end in `+clerk_test`, not contain it)\n\nFor test addresses:\n- **No real email is sent.** The OTP code is fixed.\n- **Always use code `424242`** to verify.\n\n### 2. Test phone pattern\n\n`+15555550100` through `+15555550199` are test phone numbers. Code `424242`\nverifies. Not used by this skill.\n\n### 3. Backend-API user creation\n\n`POST /v1/users` works without OTP / waitlist friction. The skill uses this\n(`clerk-backend.mjs ensure-user`) to provision users that the UI sign-up flow\nwould otherwise reject (e.g., when the Clerk dashboard has waitlist mode on).\n\n## Why this matters for Lightfast\n\nLightfast's dev Clerk tenant has **waitlist mode enabled** — fresh users can\nsign up but the OTP step returns `sign_up_restricted_waitlist`. The skill\nsidesteps this by:\n\n1. Backend API creates the user (bypasses waitlist)\n2. Browser drives `/sign-in` with the now-existing email + 424242 (works because\n   test mode treats `+clerk_test@` emails specially)\n\nWithout backend provisioning, only invited users can complete sign-up. The\nskill makes that requirement transparent.\n\n## Reading\n\n- Clerk Testing docs: https://clerk.com/docs/testing/test-emails-and-phones\n- Clerk Backend API reference: https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend-api\n- The skill's wrapper: `.agents/skills/lightfast-clerk/lib/clerk-backend.mjs`\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/jeevanpillay/Code/@lightfastai/lightfast/.agents/skills/lightfast-clerk/references/jwt-templates.md",
  "content": "# JWT templates\n\nClerk lets you mint custom JWTs from the same session via [JWT templates](https://clerk.com/docs/backend-requests/making/jwt-templates).\nThis skill supports passing a template name to `token.sh` / `curl.sh`.\n\n## Templates Lightfast uses\n\n### `lightfast-desktop`\n\nFor the Electron desktop app (Phase 4-7 of `2026-04-23-desktop-clerk-trpc-wiring.md`).\n\n- **Expiry**: `3600` seconds (1 hour)\n- **Claims**: `{ \"org_id\": \"{{org.id}}\" }` (default Clerk claim — null if user has no active org)\n- **Signing**: default (HS256, verifies via `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`)\n\nThis template **must be created manually in the Clerk Dashboard once per\nenvironment** (dev, prod). The skill cannot create templates programmatically.\n\n### Default (no template)\n\n`token.sh <profile>` (no second arg) mints a standard Clerk session JWT:\n- Short-lived (~60s by default)\n- Same claims as the session cookie\n\nUseful for testing what the web app sees from cookie-auth requests.\n\n## Behavior gotcha\n\nDefault-template JWTs (no `org_id` claim) cause the Lightfast middleware to\ntreat the request as `pending` and 307-redirect to `/account/welcome` — even\nthough `resolveClerkSession` would have accepted the JWT at the route level.\n\nThis is `proxy.ts` running auth() and finding `sessionStatus === \"pending\"`,\nwhich is independent of Bearer-vs-cookie. Use `lightfast-desktop` for tRPC\ncalls — it explicitly carries `org_id` and bypasses the redirect.\n\n```bash\n# Will 307 to /account/welcome:\n.agents/skills/lightfast-clerk/command/curl.sh claude-default account.get\n\n# Will return 200:\n.agents/skills/lightfast-clerk/command/curl.sh -t lightfast-desktop claude-default account.get\n```\n\n## Adding a new template\n\n1. Clerk Dashboard → JWT Templates → New\n2. Name it (e.g., `lightfast-cli`)\n3. Set expiry + claims\n4. Document it here\n\nThen call: `token.sh <profile> lightfast-cli` or `curl.sh -t lightfast-cli ...`\n"
}

> AGENT

Phase 1 done, skill shipped. Summary:

## Phase 1 — closed

Server-side Bearer support in `api/app/src/trpc.ts` + unit tests (5/5 green) + E2E verification via real Clerk. Valid `lightfast-desktop` JWT → HTTP 200 with profile JSON.

## `lightfast-clerk` skill — shipped at `.agents/skills/lightfast-clerk/`

7 commands tested against the real dev stack:

| Command | Verified |
|---|---|
| `token.sh <profile> [template]` | Mints JWT via Clerk Backend API, no browser |
| `login.sh <profile>` | Provisions user + browser sign-in (email + OTP 424242) |
| `status.sh <profile>` | UNKNOWN / PROVISIONED / SIGNED_IN / SIGNED_OUT |
| `signout.sh <profile>` | Server-side Clerk.signOut(), profile kept |
| `reset.sh <profile>` | rm -rf profile + meta |
| `delete-user.sh <profile>` | Backend user delete + reset |
| `curl.sh [-t tpl] <profile> <proc> [body]` | Mint + curl in one step |

Guardrails: refuses `pk_live_*`, refuses non-localhost without env override, locks profile names to `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`, `login.sh` requires `+clerk_test@` emails. Profiles gitignored at `.agent-browser/profiles/`. Symlinked into `.claude/skills/`.

## Finding to flag for later phases

Clerk middleware (`proxy.ts:72-80`) shields the tRPC route from ever seeing an invalid Bearer cleanly:

- `Bearer foo` / truncated JWT / no auth → **307** to `/sign-in`
- JWT-shaped unparseable → **500**
- Valid Bearer → **200** ✅

Phase 5's renderer 401 handler (`code === "UNAUTHORIZED"`) won't trigger on 307/500. Fix options for Phase 4–5:
- (a) expand the handler to treat 307/500 as re-auth signals, or
- (b) add `/api/trpc/(.*)` to `isApiRoute` in `proxy.ts` so middleware skips auth → route returns a proper `UNAUTHORIZED`

Documented in the plan under Phase 1's Manual Verification section.

241	- Line 91–94: `headers` callback becomes `async` and awaits the result.
242	- Line 95–100: make `credentials: 'include'` conditional — omit when the request URL origin differs from the document origin (or always-omit when no document exists).

274	#### 2.2 Add `DesktopTRPCProvider`
275	
276	**File**: `packages/app-trpc/src/desktop.tsx` (new)
277	**Changes**: New file — thin wrapper that takes `baseUrl` as a required prop (the shared package stays transport-agnostic and does NOT read Vite env vars directly) and reads the JWT from `window.lightfastBridge.auth.getToken()`. Sets `x-trpc-source: "desktop"` by returning it from `getAuthHeaders`. No `"use client"` directive — Electron has no RSC boundary, so the directive would be dead signal.
278	
279	```tsx
280	import type { ReactNode } from "react";
281	import { TRPCReactProvider } from "./react";
282	
283	interface DesktopTRPCProviderProps {
284	  children: ReactNode;
285	  baseUrl: string;
286	}
287	
288	export function DesktopTRPCProvider({ children, baseUrl }: DesktopTRPCProviderProps) {
289	  return (
290	    <TRPCReactProvider
291	      options={{
292	        baseUrl,
293	        getAuthHeaders: async () => {
294	          const token = await window.lightfastBridge.auth?.getToken();
295	          const headers: Record<string, string> = {
296	            "x-trpc-source": "desktop",
297	          };
298	          if (token) {
299	            headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
300	          }
301	          return headers;
302	        },
303	      }}
304	    >
305	      {children}
306	    </TRPCReactProvider>
307	  );
308	}
309	```
310	
311	> **Why no env read in shared package**: coupling `@repo/app-trpc` to `VITE_LIGHTFAST_API_URL` makes the package Vite-specific. Consumers should own env resolution — `apps/desktop` reads `import.meta.env.VITE_LIGHTFAST_API_URL` at its entrypoint and passes the result as a prop. This keeps the package reusable for any bundler.

1	"use client";

3	import type { AppRouter } from "@api/app";
4	import type { QueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
5	import { MutationCache, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
6	import {
7	  createTRPCClient,
8	  httpBatchStreamLink,
9	  loggerLink,
10	  TRPCClientError,
11	} from "@trpc/client";
12	import { createTRPCContext } from "@trpc/tanstack-react-query";
13	import { useState } from "react";
14	import { toast } from "sonner";
15	import SuperJSON from "superjson";
16	import { createQueryClient } from "./client";
17	
18	export interface CreateTRPCReactProviderOptions {
19	  baseUrl?: string;
20	  getAuthHeaders?: () => Record<string, string>;
21	}
22	
23	const trpcContext = createTRPCContext<AppRouter>();
24	
25	export const useTRPC = trpcContext.useTRPC;
26	export const TRPCProvider = trpcContext.TRPCProvider;
27	
28	const mutationCache = new MutationCache({
29	  onError: (error, _variables, _context, mutation) => {
30	    if (mutation.options.meta?.suppressErrorToast) {
31	      return;
32	    }
33	
34	    const title = mutation.options.meta?.errorTitle ?? "Something went wrong";
35	
36	    let message = "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again.";
37	    if (
38	      error instanceof TRPCClientError &&
39	      error.data?.httpStatus != null &&
40	      error.data.httpStatus < 500
41	    ) {
42	      message = error.message;
43	    }
44	
45	    toast.error(title, { description: message });
46	  },
47	});
48	
49	let clientQueryClientSingleton: QueryClient | undefined;
50	
51	function getQueryClient() {
52	  if (typeof window === "undefined") {
53	    return createQueryClient();
54	  }
55	
56	  return (clientQueryClientSingleton ??= createQueryClient({ mutationCache }));
57	}
58	
59	function defaultGetBaseUrl() {
60	  if (typeof window !== "undefined") {
61	    return window.location.origin;
62	  }
63	  if (process.env.VERCEL_URL) {
64	    return `https://${process.env.VERCEL_URL}`;
65	  }
66	  return `http://localhost:${process.env.PORT ?? 4104}`;
67	}
68	
69	export function TRPCReactProvider({
70	  children,
71	  options,
72	}: {
73	  children: React.ReactNode;
74	  options?: CreateTRPCReactProviderOptions;
75	}) {
76	  const queryClient = getQueryClient();
77	
78	  const [trpcClient] = useState(() => {
79	    const baseUrl = options?.baseUrl ?? defaultGetBaseUrl();
80	
81	    return createTRPCClient<AppRouter>({
82	      links: [
83	        loggerLink({
84	          enabled: (op) =>
85	            process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" ||
86	            (op.direction === "down" && op.result instanceof Error),
87	        }),
88	        httpBatchStreamLink({
89	          transformer: SuperJSON,
90	          url: `${baseUrl}/api/trpc`,
91	          headers: () => ({
92	            "x-trpc-source": "client",
93	            ...(options?.getAuthHeaders?.() ?? {}),
94	          }),
95	          fetch(url, init) {
96	            return fetch(url, {
97	              ...init,
98	              credentials: "include",
99	            } as RequestInit);
100	          },
101	        }),
102	      ],
103	    });
104	  });
105	
106	  return (
107	    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
108	      <TRPCProvider queryClient={queryClient} trpcClient={trpcClient}>
109	        {children}
110	      </TRPCProvider>
111	    </QueryClientProvider>
112	  );
113	}
114

```
344	## Phase 3: Web — shared `ClientAuthBridge` + `/desktop/auth` route
345	
346	### Overview
347	
348	The existing `cli-auth-client.tsx` and a new desktop bridge share ~90% of their logic: same `useAuth` flow, same status machine, same Suspense wrapper, same error UI. Rather than duplicate, extract a shared `ClientAuthBridge` component that both CLI and desktop consume. This collapses two sibling components into one and makes the pattern reusable for any future OAuth bridge (e.g., VS Code extension, other CLIs).
349	
350	### Changes Required
351	
352	#### 3.1 Extract shared `ClientAuthBridge`
353	
354	**File**: `apps/app/src/app/(app)/(user)/(pending-not-allowed)/_components/client-auth-bridge.tsx` (new)
355	
356	Generic bridge taking a `buildRedirectUrl` callback and an optional `jwtTemplate`. Contains all the status/UI logic from the current `cli-auth-client.tsx`.
357	
358	```tsx
359	"use client";
360	
361	import { useAuth } from "@vendor/clerk/client";
362	import { useSearchParams } from "next/navigation";
363	import { Suspense, useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
364	
365	export interface ClientAuthBridgeProps {
366	  /**
367	   * Build the redirect URL given the Clerk token.
368	   * Return null to signal invalid/missing required params — bridge renders error.
369	   */
370	  buildRedirectUrl: (args: {
371	    token: string;
372	    searchParams: URLSearchParams;
373	  }) => string | null;
374	
375	  /** Optional Clerk JWT template. Omit for default session JWT (CLI uses default). */
376	  jwtTemplate?: string;
377	
378	  /** Title shown while authenticating/redirecting. */
379	  title: string;
380	
381	  /** Body copy under the title. */
382	  subtitle: string;
383	
384	  /** Optional loading UI override (defaults to title+subtitle). */
385	  fallback?: ReactNode;
386	}
387	
388	function BridgeContent(props: ClientAuthBridgeProps) {
389	  const { getToken, isSignedIn, isLoaded } = useAuth();
390	  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
391	  const [status, setStatus] = useState<"loading" | "redirecting" | "error">(
392	    "loading"
393	  );
394	
395	  useEffect(() => {
396	    if (!isLoaded || !isSignedIn) return;
397	    void (async () => {
398	      try {
399	        const token = await getToken(
400	          props.jwtTemplate ? { template: props.jwtTemplate } : undefined
401	        );
402	        if (!token) {
403	          setStatus("error");
404	          return;
405	        }
406	        const url = props.buildRedirectUrl({ token, searchParams });
407	        if (!url) {
408	          setStatus("error");
409	          return;
410	        }
411	        setStatus("redirecting");
412	        window.location.href = url;
413	      } catch {
414	        setStatus("error");
415	      }
416	    })();
417	  }, [isLoaded, isSignedIn, getToken, props, searchParams]);
418	
419	  if (status === "error") {
420	    return (
421	      <div className="flex min-h-full items-center justify-center">
422	        <div className="text-center">
423	          <h1 className="font-semibold text-xl">Authentication Failed</h1>
424	          <p className="mt-2 text-muted-foreground">
425	            Invalid parameters. Please try again from the Lightfast app.
426	          </p>
427	        </div>
428	      </div>
429	    );
430	  }
431	
432	  return (
433	    <div className="flex min-h-full items-center justify-center">
434	      <div className="text-center">
435	        <h1 className="font-semibold text-xl">
436	          {status === "redirecting" ? "Opening Lightfast…" : props.title}
437	        </h1>
438	        <p className="mt-2 text-muted-foreground">{props.subtitle}</p>
439	      </div>
440	    </div>
441	  );
442	}
443	
444	export function ClientAuthBridge(props: ClientAuthBridgeProps) {
445	  return (
446	    <Suspense fallback={props.fallback ?? null}>
447	      <BridgeContent {...props} />
448	    </Suspense>
449	  );
450	}
451	```
452	
453	#### 3.2 Refactor `cli-auth-client.tsx` to use the bridge
454	
455	**File**: `apps/app/src/app/(app)/(user)/(pending-not-allowed)/cli/auth/_components/cli-auth-client.tsx`
456	**Changes**: Replace the entire file with a thin ~20-line consumer of `ClientAuthBridge`. No functional change to the CLI flow.
457	
458	```tsx
459	"use client";
460	
461	import { ClientAuthBridge } from "../../../_components/client-auth-bridge";
462	
463	export function CLIAuthClient() {
464	  return (
465	    <ClientAuthBridge
466	      title="Authenticating…"
467	      subtitle="You'll be redirected back to the CLI shortly."
468	      buildRedirectUrl={({ token, searchParams }) => {
469	        const port = searchParams.get("port");
470	        const state = searchParams.get("state");
471	        if (!port || !state) return null;
472	        const portNum = Number.parseInt(port, 10);
473	        if (!Number.isInteger(portNum) || portNum < 1024 || portNum > 65535) {
474	          return null;
475	        }
476	        return `http://localhost:${portNum}/callback?token=${encodeURIComponent(
477	          token
478	        )}&state=${encodeURIComponent(state)}`;
479	      }}
480	    />
481	  );
482	}
483	```
484	
485	#### 3.3 Add `/desktop/auth` route
486	
487	**File**: `apps/app/src/app/(app)/(user)/(pending-not-allowed)/desktop/auth/page.tsx` (new)
488	
489	```tsx
490	import { DesktopAuthClient } from "./_components/desktop-auth-client";
491	
492	export default function DesktopAuthPage() {
493	  return <DesktopAuthClient />;
494	}

  "file_path": "/Users/jeevanpillay/Code/@lightfastai/lightfast/apps/app/src/app/(app)/(user)/(pending-not-allowed)/_components/client-auth-bridge.tsx",
  "content": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { useAuth } from \"@vendor/clerk/client\";\nimport { useSearchParams } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { Suspense, useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from \"react\";\n\nexport interface ClientAuthBridgeProps {\n  buildRedirectUrl: (args: {\n    token: string;\n    searchParams: URLSearchParams;\n  }) => string | null;\n  jwtTemplate?: string;\n  title: string;\n  subtitle: string;\n  fallback?: ReactNode;\n}\n\nfunction BridgeContent(props: ClientAuthBridgeProps) {\n  const { getToken, isSignedIn, isLoaded } = useAuth();\n  const searchParams = useSearchParams();\n  const [status, setStatus] = useState<\"loading\" | \"redirecting\" | \"error\">(\n    \"loading\"\n  );\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!isLoaded || !isSignedIn) return;\n    void (async () => {\n      try {\n        const token = await getToken(\n          props.jwtTemplate ? { template: props.jwtTemplate } : undefined\n        );\n        if (!token) {\n          setStatus(\"error\");\n          return;\n        }\n        const url = props.buildRedirectUrl({ token, searchParams });\n        if (!url) {\n          setStatus(\"error\");\n          return;\n        }\n        setStatus(\"redirecting\");\n        window.location.href = url;\n      } catch {\n        setStatus(\"error\");\n      }\n    })();\n  }, [isLoaded, isSignedIn, getToken, props, searchParams]);\n\n  if (status === \"error\") {\n    return (\n      <div className=\"flex min-h-full items-center justify-center\">\n        <div className=\"text-center\">\n          <h1 className=\"font-semibold text-xl\">Authentication Failed</h1>\n          <p className=\"mt-2 text-muted-foreground\">\n            Invalid parameters. Please try again from the Lightfast app.\n          </p>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n    );\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"flex min-h-full items-center justify-center\">\n      <div className=\"text-center\">\n        <h1 className=\"font-semibold text-xl\">\n          {status === \"redirecting\" ? \"Opening Lightfast…\" : props.title}\n        </h1>\n        <p className=\"mt-2 text-muted-foreground\">{props.subtitle}</p>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nexport function ClientAuthBridge(props: ClientAuthBridgeProps) {\n  return (\n    <Suspense fallback={props.fallback ?? null}>\n      <BridgeContent {...props} />\n    </Suspense>\n  );\n}\n"
}

535	## Phase 4: Desktop main process — auth store, BrowserWindow sign-in, IPC, CSP
536	
537	### Overview
538	
539	Main process changes: store tokens in `safeStorage`, drive sign-in via an Electron `BrowserWindow` with a persistent partition (confirmed viable by spike, see Improvement Log), expose auth surface on `LightfastBridge`, extend CSP for API + Clerk origins. The custom `lightfast://` protocol handler (`protocol.ts`) is kept as an external-deep-link fallback but is **not** load-bearing for the sign-in happy path — we intercept `lightfast://auth/callback` inside the BrowserWindow via `session.webRequest.onBeforeRequest`, so the callback never escapes to the OS.
540	
541	> **Why BrowserWindow instead of `shell.openExternal`**: Electron BrowserWindow partitions have their own cookie jar, separate from the user's default browser. Using `shell.openExternal` means Clerk's session cookie lives in Chrome/Safari and is unreachable from Electron — forcing the user to click "Sign in" every time the JWT expires (~1h). Driving sign-in through an in-Electron BrowserWindow (visible on first sign-in, hidden for silent refresh in Phase 7) persists Clerk's session cookie to Electron's userData, enabling seamless JWT refresh for the lifetime of the Clerk session (days). The spike report (179 LOC, zero new deps) is the evidence base.
542	
543	### Changes Required
544	
545	#### 4.1 Auth store with `safeStorage`
546	
547	**File**: `apps/desktop/src/main/auth-store.ts` (new)
548	
549	Mirrors `settings-store.ts` faithfully: Zod-validated on read, try/catch on write with `console.error`, `safeStorage` encrypts payload at rest.
550	
551	```ts
552	import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, rmSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
553	import { join } from "node:path";
554	import { app, safeStorage } from "electron";
555	import { z } from "zod";
556	
557	const persistedSchema = z.object({
558	  token: z.string().min(1),
559	  savedAt: z.number().int().positive(),
560	});
561	type Persisted = z.infer<typeof persistedSchema>;
562	
563	export interface AuthSnapshot {
564	  isSignedIn: boolean;
565	}
566	
567	let memory: string | null = null;
568	const listeners = new Set<(snapshot: AuthSnapshot) => void>();
569	
570	function storePath(): string {
571	  return join(app.getPath("userData"), "auth.bin");
572	}
573	
574	function load(): string | null {
575	  if (memory) return memory;
576	  const path = storePath();
577	  if (!existsSync(path)) return null;
578	  if (!safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) return null;
579	  try {
580	    const buf = readFileSync(path);
581	    const plain = safeStorage.decryptString(buf);
582	    const parsed = persistedSchema.safeParse(JSON.parse(plain));
583	    if (!parsed.success) {
584	      console.error("auth-store: invalid persisted payload", parsed.error);
585	      return null;
586	    }
587	    memory = parsed.data.token;
588	    return memory;
589	  } catch (err) {
590	    console.error("auth-store: failed to load", err);
591	    return null;
592	  }
593	}
594	
595	function persist(token: string): void {
596	  if (!safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) {
597	    console.error("auth-store: safeStorage unavailable; refusing to write plaintext");
598	    return;
599	  }
600	  try {
601	    const payload: Persisted = { token, savedAt: Date.now() };
602	    const buf = safeStorage.encryptString(JSON.stringify(payload));
603	    writeFileSync(storePath(), buf);
604	    memory = token;
605	  } catch (err) {
606	    console.error("auth-store: failed to persist", err);
607	  }
608	}
609	
610	function clearPersisted(): void {
611	  memory = null;
612	  try {
613	    rmSync(storePath(), { force: true });
614	  } catch (err) {
615	    console.error("auth-store: failed to remove", err);
616	  }
617	}
618	
619	function emit(): void {
620	  const snapshot: AuthSnapshot = { isSignedIn: memory !== null };
621	  for (const listener of listeners) listener(snapshot);
622	}
623	
624	export function getAuthSnapshot(): AuthSnapshot {
625	  if (memory === null) load();
626	  return { isSignedIn: memory !== null };
627	}
628	
629	export function getToken(): string | null {
630	  if (memory === null) load();
631	  return memory;
632	}
633	
634	export function setToken(token: string): void {
635	  persist(token);
636	  emit();
637	}
638	
639	export function signOut(): void {
640	  clearPersisted();
641	  emit();
642	}
643	
644	export function onAuthChanged(
645	  listener: (snapshot: AuthSnapshot) => void
646	): () => void {
647	  listeners.add(listener);
648	  return () => listeners.delete(listener);
649	}
650	```
651	
652	#### 4.2 BrowserWindow-based sign-in flow
653	
654	**File**: `apps/desktop/src/main/auth-flow.ts` (new)
655	
656	Spike-validated pattern (`.claude/worktrees/agent-a99c5cfc/apps/desktop/src/main/auth-flow-spike.ts` is the reference implementation). Opens a `BrowserWindow` bound to the `persist:lightfast-auth` session partition, navigates to `/desktop/auth?state=<hex>`, and intercepts the `lightfast://auth/callback` redirect via BOTH `will-navigate` and `session.webRequest.onBeforeRequest` (dual-channel because programmatic `window.location =` navigations don't always fire `will-navigate` reliably). Exported in two flavors — `beginSignIn()` (visible, first sign-in) and `silentRefresh()` (hidden, used in Phase 7).
657	
658	```ts
659	import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
660	import { BrowserWindow, session } from "electron";
661	import { setToken } from "./auth-store";
662	
663	const API_ORIGIN =
664	  process.env.LIGHTFAST_API_URL ??
665	  (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"
666	    ? "https://lightfast.ai"
667	    : "http://localhost:3024"); // microfrontends mesh, NOT raw apps/app (4107)
668	
669	const CALLBACK_SCHEME = "lightfast";
670	const PARTITION = "persist:lightfast-auth";
671	const SIGNIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60_000; // visible flow — user-paced
672	const REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000; // hidden flow — must fail fast
673	
674	interface CallbackResult {
675	  token: string;
676	  state: string;
677	}
678	
679	function parseCallback(url: string): CallbackResult | null {
680	  try {
681	    const parsed = new URL(url);
682	    if (parsed.protocol !== `${CALLBACK_SCHEME}:`) return null;
683	    if (parsed.host !== "auth") return null;
684	    if (parsed.pathname !== "/callback") return null;
685	    const token = parsed.searchParams.get("token");
686	    const state = parsed.searchParams.get("state");
687	    if (!token || !state) return null;
688	    return { token, state };
689	  } catch {
690	    return null;
691	  }
692	}
693	
694	async function runAuthWindow(options: {
695	  visible: boolean;
696	  timeoutMs: number;
697	}): Promise<string | null> {
698	  const state = randomBytes(32).toString("hex");
699	  const partition = session.fromPartition(PARTITION);
700	  const win = new BrowserWindow({
701	    show: options.visible,
702	    width: 480,
703	    height: 720,
704	    webPreferences: { session: partition, contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false },
705	  });
706	
707	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
708	    let settled = false;
709	    const settle = (result: CallbackResult | null) => {
710	      if (settled) return;
711	      settled = true;
712	      clearTimeout(timer);
713	      partition.webRequest.onBeforeRequest(
714	        { urls: [`${CALLBACK_SCHEME}://*/*`] },
715	        null,
716	      );
717	      if (!win.isDestroyed()) win.close();
718	      if (result && result.state === state) {
719	        setToken(result.token);
720	        resolve(result.token);
721	      } else {
722	        resolve(null);
723	      }
724	    };
725	
726	    const timer = setTimeout(() => settle(null), options.timeoutMs);
727	
728	    partition.webRequest.onBeforeRequest(
729	      { urls: [`${CALLBACK_SCHEME}://*/*`] },
730	      (details, callback) => {
731	        callback({ cancel: true });
732	        settle(parseCallback(details.url));
733	      },
734	    );
735	
736	    win.webContents.on("will-navigate", (event, url) => {
737	      if (!url.startsWith(`${CALLBACK_SCHEME}://`)) return;
738	      event.preventDefault();
739	      settle(parseCallback(url));
740	    });
741	
742	    win.on("closed", () => settle(null));
743	
744	    void win.loadURL(
745	      `${API_ORIGIN}/desktop/auth?state=${encodeURIComponent(state)}`,
746	    );
747	  });
748	}
749	
750	export async function beginSignIn(): Promise<string | null> {
751	  return runAuthWindow({ visible: true, timeoutMs: SIGNIN_TIMEOUT_MS });
752	}
753	
754	export async function silentRefresh(): Promise<string | null> {
755	  return runAuthWindow({ visible: false, timeoutMs: REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS });
756	}
757	```
758	
759	> **What happened to the custom-protocol deep-link handler?** `apps/desktop/src/main/protocol.ts` and `CFBundleURLTypes` in `forge.config.ts` stay as-is — they handle the edge case where an external app invokes `lightfast://` (email links, notifications). They are **no longer load-bearing for sign-in**: the happy path intercepts `lightfast://auth/callback` inside the BrowserWindow before it escapes. The existing placeholder deep-link handler at `src/main/index.ts:321–329` (which broadcasts to all windows) can be replaced with a no-op or simple logger — we no longer need it for auth.

866	#### 4.6 CSP `connect-src` (moved from Phase 6)
867	
868	**File**: `apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts:43–64`
869	**Changes**: extend `connect-src` to include the API origin + Clerk's frontend API. The Clerk domain is derived from `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` via the existing helper `getClerkFrontendApi()` (`vendor/clerk/src/env.ts:33–57`) — do NOT hardcode a wildcard like `*.clerk.accounts.dev`, because production publishable keys decode to custom domains like `clerk.lightfast.ai`.
870	
871	```ts
872	import { getClerkFrontendApi } from "@vendor/clerk/env";
873	
874	function buildContentSecurityPolicy(): string {
875	  const apiOrigin =
876	    process.env.LIGHTFAST_API_URL ??
877	    (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"
878	      ? "https://lightfast.ai"
879	      : "http://localhost:3024"); // microfrontends mesh, NOT raw apps/app (4107)
880	  const clerkOrigin = getClerkFrontendApi(); // decodes pk_ → https://<domain>
881	
882	  const devServer = MAIN_WINDOW_VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL;
883	  if (devServer) {
884	    const origin = new URL(devServer).origin;
885	    const wsOrigin = origin.replace(/^http/, "ws");
886	    return [
887	      `default-src 'self' ${origin}`,
888	      `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' ${origin}`,
889	      `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' ${origin}`,
890	      `connect-src 'self' ${origin} ${wsOrigin} ${apiOrigin} ${clerkOrigin}`,
891	      `img-src 'self' data: blob: ${origin}`,
892	      `font-src 'self' data: ${origin}`,
893	    ].join("; ");
894	  }
895	  return [
896	    "default-src 'self'",
897	    "script-src 'self'",
898	    "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
899	    `connect-src 'self' ${apiOrigin} ${clerkOrigin}`,
900	    "img-src 'self' data: blob:",
901	    "font-src 'self' data:",
902	  ].join("; ");
903	}
904	```
905	
906	> **Note on BrowserWindow CSP**: the sign-in BrowserWindow loads `http://localhost:3024/desktop/auth` (or `https://lightfast.ai` in prod) — a top-level navigation to an external origin. CSP applies to the *renderer window's document*, not to external URLs the user navigates to. So extending `connect-src` only matters for XHR/fetch/WS the React renderer makes to the API; the BrowserWindow sign-in page is governed by the web app's own CSP, not the desktop's.

43	function buildContentSecurityPolicy(): string {

50	      `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' ${origin}`,

52	      `connect-src 'self' ${origin} ${wsOrigin}`,
53	      `img-src 'self' data: blob: ${origin}`,
54	      `font-src 'self' data: ${origin}`,
55	    ].join("; ");
56	  }
57	  return [

59	    "script-src 'self'",

1	import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
2	import { join } from "node:path";
3	import { app } from "electron";
4	import { z } from "zod";
5	
6	export const themeSourceSchema = z.enum(["system", "light", "dark"]);
7	export type ThemeSource = z.infer<typeof themeSourceSchema>;
8	
9	export const settingsSchema = z.object({
10	  themeSource: themeSourceSchema,
11	  launchAtLogin: z.boolean(),
12	  showInMenuBar: z.boolean(),
13	  checkForUpdatesAutomatically: z.boolean(),
14	});
15	
16	export type SettingsSnapshot = z.infer<typeof settingsSchema>;
17	
18	const DEFAULTS: SettingsSnapshot = {
19	  themeSource: "system",
20	  launchAtLogin: false,
21	  showInMenuBar: true,
22	  checkForUpdatesAutomatically: true,
23	};
24	
25	type Listener = (snapshot: SettingsSnapshot) => void;
26	
27	let cached: SettingsSnapshot | null = null;
28	const listeners = new Set<Listener>();
29	
30	function storePath(): string {
31	  return join(app.getPath("userData"), "settings.json");
32	}
33	
34	function read(): SettingsSnapshot {
35	  try {
36	    const raw = readFileSync(storePath(), "utf8");
37	    const parsed = settingsSchema.safeParse(JSON.parse(raw));
38	    if (parsed.success) {
39	      return parsed.data;
40	    }
41	  } catch {
42	    // file missing or malformed — fall back to defaults
43	  }
44	  return DEFAULTS;
45	}
46	
47	function write(snapshot: SettingsSnapshot): void {
48	  try {
49	    writeFileSync(storePath(), JSON.stringify(snapshot, null, 2), "utf8");
50	  } catch (error) {
51	    console.error("[settings] failed to write", error);
52	  }
53	}
54	
55	export function getSettings(): SettingsSnapshot {
56	  if (!cached) {
57	    cached = read();
58	  }
59	  return cached;
60	}
61	
62	export function updateSetting<K extends keyof SettingsSnapshot>(
63	  key: K,
64	  value: SettingsSnapshot[K]
65	): SettingsSnapshot {
66	  const next = { ...getSettings(), [key]: value };
67	  const parsed = settingsSchema.safeParse(next);
68	  if (!parsed.success) {
69	    return getSettings();
70	  }
71	  cached = parsed.data;
72	  write(parsed.data);
73	  for (const listener of listeners) {
74	    listener(parsed.data);
75	  }
76	  return parsed.data;
77	}
78	
79	export function onSettingsChanged(listener: Listener): () => void {
80	  listeners.add(listener);
81	  return () => listeners.delete(listener);
82	}
83

1	import { app, type BrowserWindow } from "electron";
2	
3	export const PROTOCOL_SCHEME = "lightfast";
4	
5	type DeepLinkHandler = (url: string) => void;
6	
7	let pendingUrl: string | null = null;
8	let handler: DeepLinkHandler | null = null;
9	
10	function deliver(url: string): void {
11	  if (handler) {
12	    handler(url);
13	  } else {
14	    pendingUrl = url;
15	  }
16	}
17	
18	export function onDeepLink(listener: DeepLinkHandler): void {
19	  handler = listener;
20	  if (pendingUrl) {
21	    listener(pendingUrl);
22	    pendingUrl = null;
23	  }
24	}
25	
26	export function registerProtocolHandler(): void {
27	  if (process.defaultApp && process.argv.length >= 2) {
28	    app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(PROTOCOL_SCHEME, process.execPath, [
29	      process.argv[1] ?? "",
30	    ]);
31	  } else {
32	    app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(PROTOCOL_SCHEME);
33	  }
34	
35	  app.on("open-url", (event, url) => {
36	    event.preventDefault();
37	    deliver(url);
38	  });
39	
40	  app.on("second-instance", (_event, argv) => {
41	    const urlArg = argv.find((arg) => arg.startsWith(`${PROTOCOL_SCHEME}://`));
42	    if (urlArg) {
43	      deliver(urlArg);
44	    }
45	  });
46	
47	  const initialUrl = process.argv.find((arg) =>
48	    arg.startsWith(`${PROTOCOL_SCHEME}://`)
49	  );
50	  if (initialUrl) {
51	    deliver(initialUrl);
52	  }
53	}
54	
55	export function focusForDeepLink(win: BrowserWindow): void {
56	  if (win.isMinimized()) {
57	    win.restore();
58	  }
59	  win.show();
60	  win.focus();
61	}
62

14	    NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY:

16	    // Note: Server variables are not included in experimental__runtimeEnv by default
17	  },
18	  skipValidation:
19	    !!process.env.SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION ||
20	    process.env.npm_lifecycle_event === "lint",
21	});

23	/**
24	 * Get the Clerk Frontend API URL from the publishable key
25	 * The publishable key contains a base64-encoded domain that we need for CSP
26	 * Format: pk_test_<base64> or pk_live_<base64>
27	 */
28	export function getClerkFrontendApi(): string {
29	  const publishableKey = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY;
30	
31	  if (!publishableKey) {
32	    // Fallback for development - this will be caught by env validation
33	    return "";
34	  }
35	
36	  // Extract the base64 part after pk_test_ or pk_live_
37	  const base64Part = publishableKey.split("_")[2];
38	
39	  if (!base64Part) {
40	    return "";
41	  }
42	
43	  try {
44	    // Decode the base64 to get the domain
45	    const decoded = Buffer.from(base64Part, "base64").toString("utf-8");
46	    // The decoded string contains the domain, extract it
47	    // Example: "charmed-shark-52.clerk.accounts.dev$"
48	    const domain = decoded.replace(/\$$/, ""); // Remove trailing $
49	    return `https://${domain}`;
50	  } catch {
51	    // If decoding fails, return empty string
52	    return "";
53	  }
54	}
55

1	/**
2	 * Spike: Clerk sign-in inside a BrowserWindow with a persistent session partition.
3	 *
4	 * Hypothesis under test:
5	 *   1. An Electron BrowserWindow with `show: false` can fully execute an external
6	 *      https:// page's JS (so Clerk can mint a JWT-template token).
7	 *   2. The navigation to `lightfast://auth/callback?token=...&state=...` can be
8	 *      intercepted BEFORE the loader tries (and fails) to resolve the custom scheme.
9	 *   3. Cookies set during the visible sign-in persist across app restarts in a
10	 *      `persist:` session partition, so subsequent silent refreshes find the
11	 *      Clerk session cookie without any UI.
12	 *
13	 * Intended usage:
14	 *   - `beginSignInInWindow()` — visible window, user completes Clerk sign-in once.
15	 *   - `silentRefresh()` — hidden window, relies on persisted Clerk __session cookie
16	 *      to immediately redirect to lightfast://auth/callback without UI.
17	 *
18	 * This file is a prototype — not wired into index.ts. It exists to prove the
19	 * API surface compiles and the interception pattern is sound.
20	 */
21	
22	import { BrowserWindow, session } from "electron";
23	import type { OnBeforeRequestListenerDetails } from "electron";
24	import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
25	
26	const AUTH_PARTITION = "persist:lightfast-auth";
27	const CALLBACK_SCHEME = "lightfast";
28	const CALLBACK_HOST = "auth";
29	const CALLBACK_PATH = "/callback";
30	const SILENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
31	
32	// Dev-mode base; prod would flip to https://lightfast.ai via env.
33	const WEB_AUTH_BASE = "http://localhost:3024/desktop/auth";
34	
35	type AuthResult = {
36	  token: string;
37	  state: string;
38	};
39	
40	function generateState(): string {
41	  return randomBytes(16).toString("hex");
42	}
43	
44	function buildAuthUrl(state: string): string {
45	  const params = new URLSearchParams({ state });
46	  return `${WEB_AUTH_BASE}?${params.toString()}`;
47	}
48	
49	/**
50	 * Matches `lightfast://auth/callback?...` and parses `token` + `state`.
```

  "content": "import { existsSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport { join } from \"node:path\";\nimport { app, safeStorage } from \"electron\";\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\n\nconst persistedSchema = z.object({\n  token: z.string().min(1),\n  savedAt: z.number().int().positive(),\n});\ntype Persisted = z.infer<typeof persistedSchema>;\n\nexport interface AuthSnapshot {\n  isSignedIn: boolean;\n}\n\nlet memory: string | null = null;\nconst listeners = new Set<(snapshot: AuthSnapshot) => void>();\n\nfunction storePath(): string {\n  return join(app.getPath(\"userData\"), \"auth.bin\");\n}\n\nfunction load(): string | null {\n  if (memory) return memory;\n  const path = storePath();\n  if (!existsSync(path)) return null;\n  if (!safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) return null;\n  try {\n    const buf = readFileSync(path);\n    const plain = safeStorage.decryptString(buf);\n    const parsed = persistedSchema.safeParse(JSON.parse(plain));\n    if (!parsed.success) {\n      console.error(\"[auth-store] invalid persisted payload\", parsed.error);\n      return null;\n    }\n    memory = parsed.data.token;\n    return memory;\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(\"[auth-store] failed to load\", err);\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction persist(token: string): void {\n  if (!safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) {\n    console.error(\n      \"[auth-store] safeStorage unavailable; refusing to write plaintext\"\n    );\n    return;\n  }\n  try {\n    const payload: Persisted = { token, savedAt: Date.now() };\n    const buf = safeStorage.encryptString(JSON.stringify(payload));\n    writeFileSync(storePath(), buf);\n    memory = token;\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(\"[auth-store] failed to persist\", err);\n  }\n}\n\nfunction clearPersisted(): void {\n  memory = null;\n  try {\n    rmSync(storePath(), { force: true });\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error(\"[auth-store] failed to remove\", err);\n  }\n}\n\nfunction emit(): void {\n  const snapshot: AuthSnapshot = { isSignedIn: memory !== null };\n  for (const listener of listeners) listener(snapshot);\n}\n\nexport function getAuthSnapshot(): AuthSnapshot {\n  if (memory === null) load();\n  return { isSignedIn: memory !== null };\n}\n\nexport function getToken(): string | null {\n  if (memory === null) load();\n  return memory;\n}\n\nexport function setToken(token: string): void {\n  persist(token);\n  emit();\n}\n\nexport function signOut(): void {\n  clearPersisted();\n  emit();\n}\n\nexport function onAuthChanged(\n  listener: (snapshot: AuthSnapshot) => void\n): () => void {\n  listeners.add(listener);\n  return () => listeners.delete(listener);\n}\n"
}

process.env.LIGHTFAST_API_URL ??\n    (process.env.NODE_ENV === \"production\"\n      ? \"https://lightfast.ai\"\n      : \"http://localhost:3024\")\n  );\n}\n\nexport interface CallbackResult {\n  token: string;\n  state: string;\n}\n\nexport function parseCallback(url: string): CallbackResult | null {\n  try {\n    const parsed = new URL(url);\n    if (parsed.protocol !== `${CALLBACK_SCHEME}:`) return null;\n    if (parsed.host !== \"auth\") return null;\n    if (parsed.pathname !== \"/callback\") return null;\n    const token = parsed.searchParams.get(\"token\");\n    const state = parsed.searchParams.get(\"state\");\n    if (!token || !state) return null;\n    return { token, state };\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nasync function runAuthWindow(options:  });\n\n  return new Promise((resolve) => {\n    let settled = false;\n\n    const settle = (result: CallbackResult | null) => {\n      if (settled) return;\n      settled = true;\n    settle(parseCallback(details.url));\n      }\n    );\n\n    win.webContents.on(\"will-navigate\", (event, url) => {\n      if (!url.startsWith(`${CALLBACK_SCHEME}://`)) return;\n   "old_string": "function buildContentSecurityPolicy(): string {\n  const devServer = MAIN_WINDOW_VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL;\n  if (devServer) {\n    const origin = new URL(devServer).origin;\n    const wsOrigin = origin.replace(/^http/, \"ws\");\n    return [\n      `default-src 'self' ${origin}`,\n      `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' ${origin}`,\n      `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' ${origin}`,\n      `connect-src 'self' ${origin} ${wsOrigin}`,\n      `img-src 'self' data: blob: ${origin}`,\n      `font-src 'self' data: ${origin}`,\n    ].join(\"; \");\n  }\n  return [\n    \"default-src 'self'\",\n    \"script-src 'self'\",\n    \"style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'\",\n    \"img-src 'self' data: blob:\",\n    \"font-src 'self' data:\",\n  ].join(\"; \");\n}",
  "new_string": "function getApiOriginForCsp(): string {\n  return (\n    process.env.LIGHTFAST_API_URL ??\n    (process.env.NODE_ENV === \"production\"\n      ? \"https://lightfast.ai\"\n      : \"http://localhost:3024\")\n  );\n}\n\nfunction getClerkFrontendApi(): string | null {\n  const publishableKey = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY;\n  if (!publishableKey) return null;\n  const base64Part = publishableKey.split(\"_\")[2];\n  if (!base64Part) return null;\n  try {\n    const domain = Buffer.from(base64Part, \"base64\")\n      .toString(\"utf-8\")\n      .replace(/\\$$/, \"\");\n    if (!domain) return null;\n    return `https://${domain}`;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction buildContentSecurityPolicy(): string {\n  const apiOrigin = getApiOriginForCsp();\n  const clerkOrigin = getClerkFrontendApi();\n  const extraConnect = [apiOrigin, clerkOrigin].filter(Boolean).join(\" \");\n\n  const devServer = MAIN_WINDOW_VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL;\n  if (devServer) {\n    const origin = new URL(devServer).origin;\n    const wsOrigin = origin.replace(/^http/, \"ws\");\n    return [\n      `default-src 'self' ${origin}`,\n      `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' ${origin}`,\n      `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' ${origin}`,\n      `connect-src 'self' ${origin} ${wsOrigin} ${extraConnect}`.trim(),\n      `img-src 'self' data: blob: ${origin}`,\n      `font-src 'self' data: ${origin}`,\n    ].join(\"; \");\n  }\n  return [\n    \"default-src 'self'\",\n    \"script-src 'self'\",\n    \"style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'\",\n    `connect-src 'self' ${extraConnect}`.trim(),\n    \"img-src 'self' data: blob:\",\n    \"font-src 'self' data:\",\n  ].join(\"; \");\n}"
}
