```json
  "new_string": "> **Note on BrowserWindow CSP**: the sign-in BrowserWindow loads `http://localhost:3024/desktop/auth` (or `https://lightfast.ai` in prod) — a top-level navigation to an external origin. CSP applies to the *renderer window's document*, not to external URLs the user navigates to. So extending `connect-src` only matters for XHR/fetch/WS the React renderer makes to the API; the BrowserWindow sign-in page is governed by the web app's own CSP, not the desktop's.\n\n> **Implementation note**: in Phase 4 execution I **inlined** a local `getClerkFrontendApi` helper in `apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts` rather than importing from `@vendor/clerk/env`. Reason: `@vendor/clerk/env` eagerly runs `@t3-oss/env-nextjs`'s `createEnv()` at module import time, which requires `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` to be set — a Next.js-only concern that would crash the Electron main process on boot. The inlined helper does exactly the same base64 decode; Phase 6 can revisit if env unification becomes desirable. The helper returns `null` when the publishable key is absent, and CSP `connect-src` silently omits the Clerk origin in that case."
}
```

Phase 4 implementation is complete and typechecks clean. Per the plan's explicit implementation note, I'm **stopping here for manual verification** before moving to Phase 5.

**What shipped**:
- `apps/desktop/src/main/auth-store.ts` — `safeStorage`-encrypted token at `userData/auth.bin`, Zod-validated, listener emitter
- `apps/desktop/src/main/auth-flow.ts` — `BrowserWindow` with `persist:lightfast-auth` partition, dual-channel intercept (`will-navigate` + `webRequest.onBeforeRequest`), `beginSignIn()` visible / `silentRefresh()` hidden, `parseCallback` exported for future tests
- `apps/desktop/src/shared/ipc.ts` — 5 new channels, `AuthSnapshot` type, `LightfastBridge.auth` subtree (`snapshot`, `getToken`, `signIn`, `signOut`, `onChanged`)
- `apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts` — IPC handlers registered; deep-link handler reduced to focus-only (auth interception now lives in `auth-flow`); `onAuthChanged` broadcast wired; CSP `connect-src` extended with `apiOrigin` + `clerkOrigin`
- `apps/desktop/src/preload/preload.ts` — `auth` subtree exposed on `lightfastBridge`

**Deviations from plan** (both documented in the plan file):
1. Inlined `getClerkFrontendApi` in `main/index.ts` instead of importing from `@vendor/clerk/env` — the Next.js env validator would crash Electron main at import time without `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`. Same 20-line base64 decode, zero runtime coupling.
2. Unit test for `parseCallback` deferred — `apps/desktop` has no test runner; adding vitest is its own infra decision. Helper is exported so the test lands later without refactoring.

**Manual verification to run when you want**:
1. Start desktop: `pnpm --filter @lightfast/desktop dev`
2. DevTools: `window.lightfastBridge.auth.snapshot` → `{ isSignedIn: false }`
3. `await window.lightfastBridge.auth.signIn()` → visible Electron BrowserWindow at `localhost:3024/desktop/auth?state=…`
4. Complete Clerk sign-in in that window → auto-close → `auth.snapshot` flips `true`
5. `ls -la ~/Library/Application\ Support/Lightfast/auth.bin` + `file auth.bin` → should report "data", not JSON
6. Relaunch app → token persists

Say when to continue to Phase 5 (renderer bootstrap + tRPC + sample call).

```
]);

// Auth routes — authenticated users should not see sign-in/sign-up forms.
const isAuthRoute = createRouteMatcher(["/sign-in(.*)", "/sign-up(.*)"]);

// Routes accessible during a pending session (signed in but has outstanding tasks
// like choosing an org). Pending users on these routes pass through to complete
// onboarding; on all other protected routes they're sent to /account/welcome.
const isPendingAllowedRoute = createRouteMatcher([
  "/account/(.*)",
  // tRPC mutations that must be callable before an org exists (e.g. creating the first org).
  // The tRPC handler's userScopedProcedure enforces its own auth; the middleware must not
  // intercept these with auth.protect() before they reach the handler.
  "/api/trpc/organization.create(.*)",
]);

export default clerkMiddleware(
  async (auth, req: NextRequest) => {
    const mfeResponse = await runMicrofrontendsMiddleware({
      request: req,
      flagValues: {},
    });
    if (mfeResponse) {
      return mfeResponse;
    }

    // Auth routes: authenticated users → /account/welcome; unauthenticated → pass through.
    if (isAuthRoute(req)) {
      const { userId } = await auth({ treatPendingAsSignedOut: false });
      if (userId) {
        return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/account/welcome", req.url));
      }
    } else if (!(isPublicRoute(req) || isApiRoute(req))) {
      const { userId, sessionStatus } = await auth({
        treatPendingAsSignedOut: false,
      });
      if (!userId) {
        const url = new URL("/sign-in", req.url);
        url.searchParams.set("redirect_url", req.nextUrl.href);
        return NextResponse.redirect(url);
      }
      if (sessionStatus === "pending" && !isPendingAllowedRoute(req)) {
        return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/account/welcome", req.url));
      }
    }

    const headersResponse = await securityHeaders();
    const response = NextResponse.next();
    for (const [key, value] of headersResponse.headers.entries()) {
      response.headers.set(key, value);
    }
```

**Verified autonomously**:

|---|---|---|
| `@lightfast/desktop` typecheck | ✅ pass | `tsc --noEmit` both tsconfigs clean |

| `auth-store` / `auth-flow` / CSP / preload load without runtime crash | ✅ pass | Boot succeeded, no `uncaughtException` / `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in logs |
| `lightfast-desktop` JWT template shape | ✅ pass | Minted via Clerk Backend API — 1h expiry (`exp-iat = 3600`), `sub = user_...`, issuer matches decoded Clerk domain, `org_id` claim present |
| `/desktop/auth` route served via mesh | ✅ pass | Build manifest shows `ƒ /desktop/auth`; 200 via `localhost:3024` with expected redirect-to-sign-in for unauth |
| CSP `connect-src` now includes API + Clerk origins | ✅ pass | Inline `getClerkFrontendApi` decoded `charmed-shark-52.clerk.accounts.dev` correctly |

**Blocked on automation**:
| Check | Why blocked |
|---|---|
| Full sign-in inside Electron BrowserWindow | `electron-forge start` needs a TTY; direct Electron boot works but driving `window.lightfastBridge.auth.signIn()` requires Chrome DevTools Protocol over `--remote-debugging-port` to execute JS in the renderer. Not wired in dev. |
| `auth.bin` written via `safeStorage.encryptString` | Requires a successful in-Electron intercept to fire `setToken`, which requires the above |
| `will-navigate` + `webRequest.onBeforeRequest` dual-channel intercept | Same as above |

**Also hit and noted**:
- `proxy.ts`'s `isPendingAllowedRoute` doesn't include `/desktop/auth` (or `/cli/auth`) — pending users get redirected to `/account/welcome` before the bridge page renders. This is a pre-existing Phase 3 / Phase 4 gap that will bite the very first desktop sign-in of any new user (everyone starts pending until they create an org). Flagging for the plan.

```
44	
45	// Routes accessible during a pending session (signed in but has outstanding tasks
46	// like choosing an org). Pending users on these routes pass through to complete
47	// onboarding; on all other protected routes they're sent to /account/welcome.
48	const isPendingAllowedRoute = createRouteMatcher([
49	  "/account/(.*)",
50	  // tRPC mutations that must be callable before an org exists (e.g. creating the first org).
51	  // The tRPC handler's userScopedProcedure enforces its own auth; the middleware must not
52	  // intercept these with auth.protect() before they reach the handler.
53	  "/api/trpc/organization.create(.*)",
54	]);

56	export default clerkMiddleware(
57	  async (auth, req: NextRequest) => {
58	    const mfeResponse = await runMicrofrontendsMiddleware({
59	      request: req,
60	      flagValues: {},
61	    });
62	    if (mfeResponse) {
63	      return mfeResponse;
64	    }
65	
66	    // Auth routes: authenticated users → /account/welcome; unauthenticated → pass through.
67	    if (isAuthRoute(req)) {
68	      const { userId } = await auth({ treatPendingAsSignedOut: false });
69	      if (userId) {
70	        return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/account/welcome", req.url));
71	      }
72	    } else if (!(isPublicRoute(req) || isApiRoute(req))) {
73	      const { userId, sessionStatus } = await auth({

75	      });

77	        const url = new URL("/sign-in", req.url);
78	        url.searchParams.set("redirect_url", req.nextUrl.href);
79	        return NextResponse.redirect(url);

81	      if (sessionStatus === "pending" && !isPendingAllowedRoute(req)) {

83	      }

85

89	      response.headers.set(key, value);
90	    }
91	    return response;
92	  },
```

535	## Phase 4: Desktop main process — auth store, BrowserWindow sign-in, IPC, CSP
536	
537	### Overview
538	
539	Main process changes: store tokens in `safeStorage`, drive sign-in via an Electron `BrowserWindow` with a persistent partition (confirmed viable by spike, see Improvement Log), expose auth surface on `LightfastBridge`, extend CSP for API + Clerk origins. The custom `lightfast://` protocol handler (`protocol.ts`) is kept as an external-deep-link fallback but is **not** load-bearing for the sign-in happy path — we intercept `lightfast://auth/callback` inside the BrowserWindow via `session.webRequest.onBeforeRequest`, so the callback never escapes to the OS.
540	
541	> **Why BrowserWindow instead of `shell.openExternal`**: Electron BrowserWindow partitions have their own cookie jar, separate from the user's default browser. Using `shell.openExternal` means Clerk's session cookie lives in Chrome/Safari and is unreachable from Electron — forcing the user to click "Sign in" every time the JWT expires (~1h). Driving sign-in through an in-Electron BrowserWindow (visible on first sign-in, hidden for silent refresh in Phase 7) persists Clerk's session cookie to Electron's userData, enabling seamless JWT refresh for the lifetime of the Clerk session (days). The spike report (179 LOC, zero new deps) is the evidence base.

```
1361	This plan was adversarially reviewed on 2026-04-23 against the current state of the codebase. Key findings and their resolutions:
1362	
1363	### Spike: Silent refresh via hidden BrowserWindow — CONFIRMED
1364	
1365	**Hypothesis**: An Electron `BrowserWindow` bound to a persistent session partition can silently re-mint JWTs by reusing Clerk's persisted `__session` cookie — visible on first sign-in, hidden for refresh. The spike-validator wrote a working 179-line prototype at `auth-flow-spike.ts` that typechecks with zero new dependencies. All three hypotheses held against Electron 33.4.11 type defs:
1366	
1367	1. `show: false` is orthogonal to navigation; cross-origin `loadURL` works.
1368	2. `session.webRequest.onBeforeRequest` with `urls: ["lightfast://*/*"]` accepts custom schemes and fires before Chromium tries to resolve them. `will-navigate` is a belt-and-suspenders fallback.
1369	3. `persist:` partitions write cookies to `userData` under `Partitions/<name>`, persisting across relaunch and isolated from the user's default browser.
1370
```

```
2	import { BrowserWindow, session } from "electron";
3	import { setToken } from "./auth-store";
4	
5	const CALLBACK_SCHEME = "lightfast";
6	const PARTITION = "persist:lightfast-auth";
7	const SIGNIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60_000;
8	const REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
9	
10	function getApiOrigin(): string {
11	  return (
12	    process.env.LIGHTFAST_API_URL ??
13	    (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"
14	      ? "https://lightfast.ai"
15	      : "http://localhost:3024")
16	  );
17	}
18	
19	export interface CallbackResult {
20	  token: string;
21	  state: string;
22	}
23	
24	export function parseCallback(url: string): CallbackResult | null {
25	  try {
26	    const parsed = new URL(url);
27	    if (parsed.protocol !== `${CALLBACK_SCHEME}:`) return null;
28	    if (parsed.host !== "auth") return null;
29	    if (parsed.pathname !== "/callback") return null;
30	    const token = parsed.searchParams.get("token");
31	    const state = parsed.searchParams.get("state");
32	    if (!token || !state) return null;
33	    return { token, state };
34	  } catch {
35	    return null;
36	  }
37	}
38	
39	async function runAuthWindow(options: {
40	  visible: boolean;
41	  timeoutMs: number;
42	}): Promise<string | null> {
43	  const state = randomBytes(32).toString("hex");
44	  const partition = session.fromPartition(PARTITION);
45	  const win = new BrowserWindow({
46	    show: options.visible,
47	    width: 480,
48	    height: 720,
49	    webPreferences: {
50	      session: partition,
51	      contextIsolation: true,
52	      nodeIntegration: false,
53	    },
54	  });
55	
56	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
57	    let settled = false;
58	
59	    const settle = (result: CallbackResult | null) => {
60	      if (settled) return;
61	      settled = true;
62	      clearTimeout(timer);
63	      partition.webRequest.onBeforeRequest(
64	        { urls: [`${CALLBACK_SCHEME}://*/*`] },
65	        null
66	      );
67	      if (!win.isDestroyed()) win.close();
68	      if (result && result.state === state) {
69	        setToken(result.token);
70	        resolve(result.token);
71	      } else {
72	        resolve(null);
73	      }
74	    };
75	
76	    const timer = setTimeout(() => settle(null), options.timeoutMs);
77	
78	    partition.webRequest.onBeforeRequest(
79	      { urls: [`${CALLBACK_SCHEME}://*/*`] },
80	      (details, callback) => {
```

**Bug fixed en route**: `session.webRequest.onBeforeRequest({urls: ["lightfast://*/*"]}, ...)` throws `TypeError: Invalid url pattern: Wrong scheme type` on Electron 33.4.11 — Chrome-extension match patterns only accept `http/https/file/ftp/urn`. Swapped for `partition.protocol.handle(CALLBACK_SCHEME, ...)` which is the documented custom-scheme intercept API. The `will-navigate` path remains primary; `protocol.handle` is the safety net. The spike worktree's claim that the dual-channel worked is incorrect as written — this would have failed at the first real sign-in in Phase 6.

Plan's Improvement Log updated with the finding. Ready for Phase 5.

906	> **Note on BrowserWindow CSP**: the sign-in BrowserWindow loads `http://localhost:3024/desktop/auth` (or `https://lightfast.ai` in prod) — a top-level navigation to an external origin. CSP applies to the *renderer window's document*, not to external URLs the user navigates to. So extending `connect-src` only matters for XHR/fetch/WS the React renderer makes to the API; the BrowserWindow sign-in page is governed by the web app's own CSP, not the desktop's.
907	
908	> **Implementation note**: in Phase 4 execution I **inlined** a local `getClerkFrontendApi` helper in `apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts` rather than importing from `@vendor/clerk/env`. Reason: `@vendor/clerk/env` eagerly runs `@t3-oss/env-nextjs`'s `createEnv()` at module import time, which requires `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` to be set — a Next.js-only concern that would crash the Electron main process on boot. The inlined helper does exactly the same base64 decode; Phase 6 can revisit if env unification becomes desirable. The helper returns `null` when the publishable key is absent, and CSP `connect-src` silently omits the Clerk origin in that case.

1022	```tsx
1023	import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
1024	import { useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
1025	import type { AuthSnapshot } from "../../../shared/ipc";
1026	import { AccountCard } from "./account-card";

1028	export function AppShell() {

1030	    () => window.lightfastBridge.auth.snapshot
1031	  );
1032	  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
1033	
1034	  useEffect(() => {
1035	    return window.lightfastBridge.auth.onChanged(setAuth);
1036	  }, []);

1038	  // Global 401 handler: if any tRPC query returns UNAUTHORIZED, the token is
1039	  // invalid/expired. Clear local auth state; Phase 7 adds silent refresh in front of this.
1040	  useEffect(() => {
1041	    const unsub = queryClient.getQueryCache().subscribe((event) => {
1042	      if (event.type !== "updated") return;

1044	      if (!err) return;

1048	      }
1049	    });
1050	    return unsub;
1051	  }, [queryClient]);
1052

1057	          type="button"
1058	          onClick={() => void window.lightfastBridge.auth.signIn()}
1059	        >

1062	      </div>
1063	    );
1064	  }
1065

1067	    <div>
1068	      <AccountCard />
1069	      <button
1070	        type="button"

1072	      >

1074	      </button>

1076	  );

1	# Desktop Clerk Auth + tRPC Wiring Implementation Plan
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Wire Clerk authentication and tRPC into `apps/desktop` (Electron Forge app). Single shared router (`@api/app`) serves both web (cookie auth) and desktop (Bearer JWT auth). Desktop signs in via system-browser OAuth → custom-protocol deep-link (`lightfast://auth/callback`) → JWT stored in Electron `safeStorage`. Renderer uses React + `@repo/app-trpc` with a new `DesktopTRPCProvider`.
6	
7	End-to-end validation: run `pnpm dev:desktop-stack` (new script — boots `dev:full` + the microfrontends proxy in one process) and `pnpm dev:desktop` concurrently. The microfrontends mesh runs on `http://localhost:3024` and fronts `apps/app` at 4107 + `apps/www` at 4101 (platform at 4112 is **not** in the mesh — it's a separate service at `platform.lightfast.ai`). Desktop signs in, calls `account.get` on the real API, renders the authenticated user's profile.
8	
9	> **Origin note**: both the tRPC route handler's CORS (`apps/app/src/app/(trpc)/api/trpc/[trpc]/route.ts:13–16`) and the prod `https://lightfast.ai` single-origin shape assume **microfrontends-mesh origin**, not the raw `apps/app` port. Desktop must hit `http://localhost:3024` in dev and `https://lightfast.ai` in prod. Hitting `http://localhost:4107` directly from the Electron renderer would fail CORS.
10	
11	> **Critical dev-stack note**: `pnpm dev:full` alone does NOT start the 3024 mesh — it only boots apps at 4107/4101/4112. Port 3024 requires the `microfrontends proxy --port 3024` command defined in `apps/app/package.json:13`, which is not in any turbo pipeline today. Phase 6.3 adds a root `dev:desktop-stack` script that runs both concurrently.
12	
13	## Current State Analysis
14	
15	### What exists
16	
17	- **`apps/desktop`** — Electron Forge app with hardened main process. Renderer is vanilla TS (no React, no HTTP client, no state lib).
18	  - `src/main/protocol.ts:3,26–53` — `lightfast://` protocol already registered via `app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient`; deep-link delivery already wired (`open-url`, `second-instance`, initial argv). `onDeepLink()` callback queues URLs until a handler is registered.
19	  - `src/main/index.ts:321–329` — current deep-link handler *misroutes* the URL onto `IpcChannels.openExternal` broadcast to every window. This is clearly a placeholder and will be replaced with a dedicated auth-callback channel.
20	  - `src/main/index.ts:43–76` — CSP. Dev `connect-src`: `'self' ${origin} ${wsOrigin}`. Production: `'self'` only. **Missing** API origin and Clerk frontend API.
21	  - `src/main/settings-store.ts` — raw JSON I/O into `userData/settings.json`, zod-validated. Pattern to mirror for token storage via `safeStorage`.
22	  - `src/shared/ipc.ts:5–22` — central `IpcChannels` enum. Add auth channels here.
23	  - `src/shared/ipc.ts:93–121` — `LightfastBridge` interface exposed via `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld("lightfastBridge", ...)` in `src/preload/preload.ts:72`.
24	  - `forge.config.ts:78–83` — `CFBundleURLTypes` already declares the `lightfast` URL scheme on macOS.
25	  - `tsconfig.json:6` — `jsx: "preserve"`. Needs switch to `"react-jsx"` for React.

27	  - `src/renderer/index.html` — single `<div id="app">` root. Hash router at `src/renderer/src/router.ts` with `"home" | "settings"` routes.

31	  - `src/client.ts` — transport-agnostic QueryClient. Reusable as-is.
32	  - `src/server.tsx` — Next.js RSC only (imports `next/headers`). Desktop does not use this.

We will mirror this pattern for desktop, swapping the localhost port redirect for `lightfast://auth/callback`.
45	
46	- **Smoke-test procedure**: `api/app/src/router/user/account.ts:29–59` — `account.get` on `userScopedProcedure` returns the signed-in user's Clerk profile. Desktop will call this post-auth.
47	
48	### Key constraints
49	
50	- **Clerk session JWTs are short-lived (~60s by default)**. For desktop we use a Clerk **JWT template** (configured in Clerk Dashboard) named `lightfast-desktop` with 1h expiry, embedding `org_id`. Web-side desktop auth page calls `getToken({ template: "lightfast-desktop" })`. On expiry, Phase 7 silently re-issues via a hidden BrowserWindow — Clerk's persisted session cookie (in the `persist:lightfast-auth` partition) is valid for days.
51	- **Single-instance lock must be active before deep-link delivery**. Already present (`src/main/bootstrap.ts:13`).
52	- **CSRF protection on the auth callback**: Since we intercept `lightfast://auth/callback` inside our own BrowserWindow (not via OS-level protocol handler for the happy path), third-party apps invoking `lightfast://auth/callback?token=STOLEN_JWT` can never reach us through the sign-in flow. Defense-in-depth: we still generate a cryptographically random `state` per sign-in and reject callbacks that don't match. The OS-level protocol handler (still registered for external deep-links) is now auth-neutral.
53	- **tRPC v11 `httpBatchStreamLink.headers`** supports both sync and async return values (Promise). Widening the `getAuthHeaders` signature is a zero-risk change.
54	- **Electron session partitioning**: `session.fromPartition("persist:lightfast-auth")` persists cookies to disk under `userData/Partitions/lightfast-auth`, isolated from the user's default browser. This is why sign-in works inside a BrowserWindow but `shell.openExternal` can never be silent — system Safari/Chrome cookies are unreachable from Electron.
55	
56	## Desired End State
57	
58	- Running `pnpm dev:desktop-stack` (mesh + apps at 3024) + `pnpm dev:desktop` concurrently:
59	  1. Desktop launches, renders a "Sign in with Lightfast" button in the primary window (React).
60	  2. Clicking the button opens a **visible Electron BrowserWindow** to `http://localhost:3024/desktop/auth?state=...` — bound to the `persist:lightfast-auth` session partition.
61	  3. BrowserWindow completes Clerk sign-in (cookie path, existing flow), calls `getToken({ template: "lightfast-desktop" })`, redirects to `lightfast://auth/callback?token=...&state=...`.
62	  4. Main process intercepts via `session.webRequest.onBeforeRequest` before the protocol escapes to the OS.
63	  5. Main process validates `state`, stores JWT via `safeStorage.encryptString`, closes the BrowserWindow, notifies renderer via IPC.
64	  6. Renderer flips to "signed in" state, calls tRPC `account.get` with `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, renders the profile.
65	  7. On token expiry (Phase 7), a hidden BrowserWindow in the same partition silently re-issues — user sees nothing.
66	- Server-side: `/api/trpc` accepts Bearer tokens for desktop clients and existing cookies for web; single `AuthContext` union, identical procedures.
67	- Web flows (sign-in, sign-up, any existing cookie-based session) are **unchanged**.

Hitting the raw `apps/app` port (4107) would require adding it to `allowedOrigins`; we deliberately avoid this to keep the dev/prod story single-origin.

84	## What We're NOT Doing
85	
86	- **Not introducing React in HUD or secondary windows.** Only the primary window gets React + tRPC this iteration.
87	- **Not refactoring the hash router.** Settings screen and existing vanilla TS UI stay.
88	- **Not building an in-app sign-up flow.** The sign-in BrowserWindow loads Clerk's existing web UI — sign-up is handled there without any desktop-side work.
89	- **Not adding biometric unlock / Touch ID gates.** `safeStorage` (keychain-backed) is the storage layer; no extra UX.
90	- **Not implementing Clerk webhook handling for session revocation.** If silent refresh fails (Clerk session itself invalidated), desktop clears the token and re-prompts sign-in.
91	- **Not adding `orgScopedProcedure` usage to desktop this iteration.** Org switching UX lands after the end-to-end Bearer path is proven.
92	- **Not refactoring `@repo/app-trpc`'s RSC surface.** `server.tsx` stays Next-only.
93	- **Not changing the observability `@vendor/observability/trpc` middleware's auth extraction** — it reads from `ctx.auth` which is unchanged.
94	- **Not using `shell.openExternal` for sign-in.** The system browser's cookie jar is unreachable from Electron, so using it would force hourly re-auth. The BrowserWindow flow is confirmed viable by the spike (see Improvement Log) and is a first-class design decision.
95	
96	## Implementation Approach
97	
98	Seven discrete, independently-landable phases. Phases 1–3 are safe to merge before any desktop changes exist (web is unaffected). Phase 4 introduces desktop main-process auth + BrowserWindow sign-in + CSP. Phase 5 introduces React in the renderer + 401 handling. Phase 6 closes the dev loop and documents setup. Phase 7 (silent refresh) wires the already-implemented `silentRefresh()` in front of the 401 handler — the spike proved it works; Phase 7 is just the renderer-side hookup.

102	## Phase 1: Server — Bearer token support in `createTRPCContext`
103	
104	### Overview
105	
106	Extend `api/app/src/trpc.ts` `createTRPCContext` to accept `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` in addition to Clerk cookies. Zero changes to `AuthContext`, procedures, or any caller.
107	
108	### Changes Required
109	
110	#### 1.1 Add `resolveClerkSession` helper
111	
112	**File**: `api/app/src/trpc.ts`
113	**Changes**: Add a private helper above `createTRPCContext` that unifies cookie + Bearer paths. Call it from `createTRPCContext` instead of `auth()`.
114	
115	```ts
116	import { auth, verifyToken } from "@vendor/clerk/server";
117	import { clerkEnvBase } from "@vendor/clerk/env";
118	
119	type ResolvedSession =
120	  | { userId: string; orgId: string | null }
121	  | null;
122	
123	async function resolveClerkSession(headers: Headers): Promise<ResolvedSession> {
124	  const authHeader = headers.get("authorization") ?? "";
125	  const match = authHeader.match(/^Bearer\s+(.+)$/i);
126	  if (match) {
127	    const jwt = match[1];
128	    try {
129	      const claims = await verifyToken(jwt, {
130	        secretKey: clerkEnvBase.CLERK_SECRET_KEY,
131	      });
132	      const userId = typeof claims.sub === "string" ? claims.sub : null;
133	      if (!userId) return null;
134	      const orgId =
135	        typeof (claims as { org_id?: unknown }).org_id === "string"
136	          ? ((claims as { org_id: string }).org_id)
137	          : null;
138	      return { userId, orgId };
139	    } catch {
140	      // Invalid/expired JWT — fall through to unauthenticated
141	      return null;
142	    }
143	  }
144	
145	  const cookieSession = await auth({ treatPendingAsSignedOut: false });
146	  if (!cookieSession.userId) return null;
147	  return {
148	    userId: cookieSession.userId,
149	    orgId: cookieSession.orgId ?? null,
150	  };
151	}
152	```
153	
154	#### 1.2 Swap the `auth()` call in `createTRPCContext`
155	
156	**File**: `api/app/src/trpc.ts:58–88`
157	**Changes**: Replace the body of `createTRPCContext` with a call to `resolveClerkSession(opts.headers)` that feeds the same `AuthContext` union.
158	
159	```ts
160	export const createTRPCContext = async (opts: { headers: Headers }) => {
161	  const session = await resolveClerkSession(opts.headers);
162	
163	  if (session) {
164	    if (session.orgId) {
165	      return {
166	        auth: {
167	          type: "clerk-active" as const,
168	          userId: session.userId,
169	          orgId: session.orgId,
170	        },
171	        db,
172	        headers: opts.headers,
173	      };
174	    }
175	    return {
176	      auth: { type: "clerk-pending" as const, userId: session.userId },
177	      db,
178	      headers: opts.headers,
179	    };
180	  }
181	
182	  return {
183	    auth: { type: "unauthenticated" as const },
184	    db,
185	    headers: opts.headers,
186	  };
187	};
188	```
189	
190	#### 1.3 Extend observability middleware `x-trpc-source` handling (optional)
191	
192	**File**: `api/app/src/trpc.ts:146–159`
193	**Changes**: None required — `x-trpc-source` values are free-form labels. Existing middleware records whatever the client sends.

277	**Changes**: New file — thin wrapper that takes `baseUrl` as a required prop (the shared package stays transport-agnostic and does NOT read Vite env vars directly) and reads the JWT from `window.lightfastBridge.auth.getToken()`. Sets `x-trpc-source: "desktop"` by returning it from `getAuthHeaders`. No `"use client"` directive — Electron has no RSC boundary, so the directive would be dead signal.

279	```tsx
280	import type { ReactNode } from "react";
281	import { TRPCReactProvider } from "./react";
282

284	  children: ReactNode;
285	  baseUrl: string;

288	export function DesktopTRPCProvider({ children, baseUrl }: DesktopTRPCProviderProps) {
289	  return (
290	    <TRPCReactProvider
291	      options={{
292	        baseUrl,
293	        getAuthHeaders: async () => {
294	          const token = await window.lightfastBridge.auth?.getToken();
295	          const headers: Record<string, string> = {
296	            "x-trpc-source": "desktop",
297	          };
298	          if (token) {
299	            headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
300	          }
301	          return headers;
302	        },
303	      }}
304	    >
305	      {children}
306	    </TRPCReactProvider>
307	  );

344	## Phase 3: Web — shared `ClientAuthBridge` + `/desktop/auth` route
345	
346	### Overview
347	
348	The existing `cli-auth-client.tsx` and a new desktop bridge share ~90% of their logic: same `useAuth` flow, same status machine, same Suspense wrapper, same error UI. Rather than duplicate, extract a shared `ClientAuthBridge` component that both CLI and desktop consume. This collapses two sibling components into one and makes the pattern reusable for any future OAuth bridge (e.g., VS Code extension, other CLIs).
349	
350	### Changes Required
351	
352	#### 3.1 Extract shared `ClientAuthBridge`
353	
354	**File**: `apps/app/src/app/(app)/(user)/(pending-not-allowed)/_components/client-auth-bridge.tsx` (new)
355	
356	Generic bridge taking a `buildRedirectUrl` callback and an optional `jwtTemplate`. Contains all the status/UI logic from the current `cli-auth-client.tsx`.
357	
358	```tsx
359	"use client";
360	
361	import { useAuth } from "@vendor/clerk/client";
362	import { useSearchParams } from "next/navigation";
363	import { Suspense, useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
364	
365	export interface ClientAuthBridgeProps {
366	  /**
367	   * Build the redirect URL given the Clerk token.
368	   * Return null to signal invalid/missing required params — bridge renders error.
369	   */
370	  buildRedirectUrl: (args: {
371	    token: string;
372	    searchParams: URLSearchParams;
373	  }) => string | null;
374	
375	  /** Optional Clerk JWT template. Omit for default session JWT (CLI uses default). */
376	  jwtTemplate?: string;
377	
378	  /** Title shown while authenticating/redirecting. */
379	  title: string;
380	
381	  /** Body copy under the title. */
382	  subtitle: string;
383	
384	  /** Optional loading UI override (defaults to title+subtitle). */
385	  fallback?: ReactNode;
386	}
387	
388	function BridgeContent(props: ClientAuthBridgeProps) {
389	  const { getToken, isSignedIn, isLoaded } = useAuth();
390	  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
391	  const [status, setStatus] = useState<"loading" | "redirecting" | "error">(
392	    "loading"
393	  );
394	
395	  useEffect(() => {
396	    if (!isLoaded || !isSignedIn) return;
397	    void (async () => {
398	      try {
399	        const token = await getToken(
400	          props.jwtTemplate ? { template: props.jwtTemplate } : undefined
401	        );
402	        if (!token) {
403	          setStatus("error");
404	          return;
405	        }
406	        const url = props.buildRedirectUrl({ token, searchParams });
407	        if (!url) {
408	          setStatus("error");
409	          return;
410	        }
411	        setStatus("redirecting");
412	        window.location.href = url;
413	      } catch {
414	        setStatus("error");
415	      }
416	    })();
417	  }, [isLoaded, isSignedIn, getToken, props, searchParams]);
418	
419	  if (status === "error") {
420	    return (
421	      <div className="flex min-h-full items-center justify-center">
422	        <div className="text-center">
423	          <h1 className="font-semibold text-xl">Authentication Failed</h1>
424	          <p className="mt-2 text-muted-foreground">
425	            Invalid parameters. Please try again from the Lightfast app.
426	          </p>
427	        </div>
428	      </div>
429	    );
430	  }
431	
432	  return (
433	    <div className="flex min-h-full items-center justify-center">
434	      <div className="text-center">
435	        <h1 className="font-semibold text-xl">
436	          {status === "redirecting" ? "Opening Lightfast…" : props.title}
437	        </h1>
438	        <p className="mt-2 text-muted-foreground">{props.subtitle}</p>
439	      </div>
440	    </div>
441	  );
442	}
443	
444	export function ClientAuthBridge(props: ClientAuthBridgeProps) {
445	  return (
446	    <Suspense fallback={props.fallback ?? null}>
447	      <BridgeContent {...props} />
448	    </Suspense>
449	  );
450	}
451	```

469	        const port = searchParams.get("port");
470	        const state = searchParams.get("state");
471	        if (!port || !state) return null;
472	        const portNum = Number.parseInt(port, 10);

534	
535	## Phase 4: Desktop main process — auth store, BrowserWindow sign-in, IPC, CSP
536	
537	### Overview
538	
539	Main process changes: store tokens in `safeStorage`, drive sign-in via an Electron `BrowserWindow` with a persistent partition (confirmed viable by spike, see Improvement Log), expose auth surface on `LightfastBridge`, extend CSP for API + Clerk origins. The custom `lightfast://` protocol handler (`protocol.ts`) is kept as an external-deep-link fallback but is **not** load-bearing for the sign-in happy path — we intercept `lightfast://auth/callback` inside the BrowserWindow via `session.webRequest.onBeforeRequest`, so the callback never escapes to the OS.
540	
541	> **Why BrowserWindow instead of `shell.openExternal`**: Electron BrowserWindow partitions have their own cookie jar, separate from the user's default browser. Using `shell.openExternal` means Clerk's session cookie lives in Chrome/Safari and is unreachable from Electron — forcing the user to click "Sign in" every time the JWT expires (~1h). Driving sign-in through an in-Electron BrowserWindow (visible on first sign-in, hidden for silent refresh in Phase 7) persists Clerk's session cookie to Electron's userData, enabling seamless JWT refresh for the lifetime of the Clerk session (days). The spike report (179 LOC, zero new deps) is the evidence base.
542	
543	### Changes Required
544	
545	#### 4.1 Auth store with `safeStorage`
546	
547	**File**: `apps/desktop/src/main/auth-store.ts` (new)
548	
549	Mirrors `settings-store.ts` faithfully: Zod-validated on read, try/catch on write with `console.error`, `safeStorage` encrypts payload at rest.
550	
551	```ts
552	import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, rmSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
553	import { join } from "node:path";
554	import { app, safeStorage } from "electron";
555	import { z } from "zod";
556	
557	const persistedSchema = z.object({
558	  token: z.string().min(1),
559	  savedAt: z.number().int().positive(),
560	});
561	type Persisted = z.infer<typeof persistedSchema>;
562	
563	export interface AuthSnapshot {
564	  isSignedIn: boolean;
565	}
566	
567	let memory: string | null = null;
568	const listeners = new Set<(snapshot: AuthSnapshot) => void>();
569	
570	function storePath(): string {
571	  return join(app.getPath("userData"), "auth.bin");
572	}
573	
574	function load(): string | null {
575	  if (memory) return memory;
576	  const path = storePath();
577	  if (!existsSync(path)) return null;
578	  if (!safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) return null;
579	  try {
580	    const buf = readFileSync(path);
581	    const plain = safeStorage.decryptString(buf);
582	    const parsed = persistedSchema.safeParse(JSON.parse(plain));
583	    if (!parsed.success) {
584	      console.error("auth-store: invalid persisted payload", parsed.error);
585	      return null;
586	    }
587	    memory = parsed.data.token;
588	    return memory;
589	  } catch (err) {
590	    console.error("auth-store: failed to load", err);
591	    return null;
592	  }
593	}
594	
595	function persist(token: string): void {
596	  if (!safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) {
597	    console.error("auth-store: safeStorage unavailable; refusing to write plaintext");
598	    return;
599	  }
```

1235	## Phase 7: Silent JWT refresh via hidden BrowserWindow
1236	
1237	### Overview
1238	
1239	By end of Phase 6, desktop works but forces re-auth every ~1h when the JWT template expires. Phase 7 wires `silentRefresh()` (already implemented in Phase 4.2's `auth-flow.ts`) in front of the 401 handler so expiry is invisible to the user. The spike-validated pattern reuses Phase 4's `persist:lightfast-auth` partition — the hidden window finds Clerk's persisted `__session` cookie, mints a fresh JWT, and settles within seconds. User sees nothing. Re-sign-in only becomes visible when the *Clerk session* expires (days, not hours).

1259	
1260	**File**: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/react/app-shell.tsx`
1261	**Changes**: replace the 401 handler's direct `signOut()` with: attempt `silentRefresh()` first; only fall back to `signOut()` if refresh returns `null`. Invalidate all queries on success so refetches use the new token.
1262	
1263	```tsx
1264	useEffect(() => {
1265	  const unsub = queryClient.getQueryCache().subscribe(async (event) => {
1266	    if (event.type !== "updated") return;
1267	    const err = event.query.state.error;
1268	    if (!err) return;
1269	    const code = (err as { data?: { code?: string } }).data?.code;
1270	    if (code !== "UNAUTHORIZED") return;
1271	
1272	    const refreshed = await window.lightfastBridge.auth.silentRefresh();
1273	    if (refreshed) {
1274	      await queryClient.invalidateQueries();
1275	    } else {
1276	      await window.lightfastBridge.auth.signOut();
1277	    }
1278	  });
1279	  return unsub;
1280	}, [queryClient]);
1281	```
1282	
1283	> **Concurrency**: a single in-flight refresh guard can be added later if multiple queries 401 simultaneously. First-ship: accept possibly-duplicate refresh calls — the hidden window is cheap, Clerk is idempotent.
1284	
1285	### Success Criteria
1286	
1287	#### Automated Verification
1288	
1289	- [ ] `pnpm --filter @lightfast/desktop typecheck` passes.
1290	
1291	#### Manual Verification
1292	
1293	- [ ] Sign in normally.
1294	- [ ] In Clerk dashboard, set JWT template expiry to 60s (or edit locally).
1295	- [ ] Wait 90s, trigger any tRPC query (e.g., refresh a page that fetches `account.get`).
1296	- [ ] Devtools: observe a `lightfast://` network trace, but no visible window appears — the hidden BrowserWindow ran and closed.
1297	- [ ] Query retries and succeeds with a fresh `Authorization: Bearer <new jwt>` header.
1298	- [ ] Kill Electron's persisted Clerk session (delete `~/Library/Application Support/Lightfast/Partitions/lightfast-auth`) → next 401 triggers silent refresh, fails (no session cookie) → falls back to `signOut()`, UI flips to signed-out.

1327	## Performance Considerations
1328	
1329	- **JWT verification cost**: `verifyToken` with `secretKey` does a symmetric signature check — µs-scale, no network. Public-key JWKS verification is not used here.
1330	- **Token refresh cost**: Phase 7's silent refresh opens a hidden BrowserWindow pointed at `/desktop/auth`. Cost: one HTML page load + one Clerk `getToken` call + one redirect. Warm case (Clerk cookie present): sub-second. Cold case (cookie missing/expired): 30s timeout → fall back to signed-out state. No persistent background timers.
1331	- **CSP evaluation**: adding origins to `connect-src` is free; no perceptible impact.
1332	- **Session partition disk footprint**: `persist:lightfast-auth` stores Clerk cookies (~few KB) + browsing cache for `*.lightfast.ai`. Trimmable via `session.fromPartition("persist:lightfast-auth").clearCache()` if ever needed — not expected.
1333	
1334	## Migration Notes
1335	
1336	- **No data migration** — desktop has no existing auth state.
1337	- **Web users unaffected** — cookie path is preserved identically.
1338	- **Rollback**: revert `api/app/src/trpc.ts` to call `auth()` directly. Desktop will stop working; web continues.

1359	## Improvement Log
1360	
1361	This plan was adversarially reviewed on 2026-04-23 against the current state of the codebase. Key findings and their resolutions:
1362	
1363	### Spike: Silent refresh via hidden BrowserWindow — CONFIRMED
1364	
1365	**Hypothesis**: An Electron `BrowserWindow` bound to a persistent session partition can silently re-mint JWTs by reusing Clerk's persisted `__session` cookie — visible on first sign-in, hidden for refresh. The spike-validator wrote a working 179-line prototype at `auth-flow-spike.ts` that typechecks with zero new dependencies. All three hypotheses held against Electron 33.4.11 type defs:
1366	
1367	1. `show: false` is orthogonal to navigation; cross-origin `loadURL` works.
1368	2. `session.webRequest.onBeforeRequest` with `urls: ["lightfast://*/*"]` accepts custom schemes and fires before Chromium tries to resolve them. `will-navigate` is a belt-and-suspenders fallback.
1369	3. `persist:` partitions write cookies to `userData` under `Partitions/<name>`, persisting across relaunch and isolated from the user's default browser.
1370	
1371	**Impact on plan**: Replaced `shell.openExternal` with `BrowserWindow`-based sign-in (Phase 4.2). Added Phase 7 for silent refresh. Removed hourly re-auth UX burden — users now re-auth only when their Clerk session itself expires (days).
1372	
1373	### Critical fixes applied
1374	
1375	- **`env` vs `clerkEnvBase` import** (Phase 1.1): plan's original `import { env } from "@vendor/clerk/env"` was broken — the actual export is `clerkEnvBase`. Fixed.
1376	- **`primaryEmail` vs `primaryEmailAddress`** (Phase 5.4): procedure returns `primaryEmailAddress`. Fixed.
1377	- **CSP wildcard vs decoded domain** (Phase 4.6): replaced `https://*.clerk.accounts.dev` wildcard with `getClerkFrontendApi()` helper — prod Clerk domains (e.g., `clerk.lightfast.ai`) don't match the wildcard.
1378	- **Microfrontends claim** (overview + Phase 6.1): plan said mesh fronts app+www+platform; platform is NOT in the mesh per `microfrontends.json`. Corrected.
1379	- **`dev:full` doesn't start 3024** (Phase 6.2): added new `dev:desktop-stack` script that starts `dev:full` AND the 3024 proxy. The proxy is only defined in `apps/app/package.json:13` and not in any turbo task.
1380	
1381	### Design changes
1382	
1383	- **`baseUrl` as prop** (Phase 2.2, 5.4): moved Vite env resolution out of `@repo/app-trpc/desktop.tsx` into `apps/desktop`'s entry. Shared package stays transport-agnostic.
1384	- **Shared `ClientAuthBridge` component** (Phase 3.1): extracted ~90% duplication between CLI and desktop auth bridges into a reusable component. CLI refactored to consume it (Phase 3.2). Future CLI/desktop/OAuth bridges get the pattern for free.
1385	- **Faithful `settings-store.ts` mirror for `auth-store.ts`** (Phase 4.1): added Zod schema for persisted payload, try/catch around `writeFileSync`, `console.error` on failure. Previously the plan diverged from the template without justification.
1386	- **CSP moved to Phase 4** (Phase 4.6): originally in Phase 6, but Phase 5's renderer tRPC calls need it — the original ordering would have broken Phase 5's manual verification.
1387	- **Channel naming convention** (Phase 4.3): renamed `authGetTokenSync` → `authGetToken`. The `*Sync` suffix is reserved for `ipcMain.on` + `event.returnValue` (matches existing `getBuildInfoSync`, `getSettingsSync` at `index.ts:114,118,122`). The plan originally registered `authGetTokenSync` with `ipcMain.handle` (async), violating the convention.
1388	- **401 handling in renderer** (Phase 5.4): `AppShell` now subscribes to the query cache and reacts to `UNAUTHORIZED` errors. Without this, a stale token would leave the UI in a broken signed-in state while every tRPC call fails. Phase 7 extends this to try `silentRefresh()` first.
1389	- **Removed `"use client"` from `desktop.tsx`** (Phase 2.2): dead signal in Electron — no RSC boundary.
1390	- **Deep-link handler simplified** (Phase 4.4): auth interception moved into BrowserWindow; `protocol.ts` + `CFBundleURLTypes` now serve only external deep-links (notifications, shared artifacts). The placeholder broadcast at `index.ts:321–329` is replaced with a focus-only no-op.
1391	
1392	### Decisions deferred
1393	
1394	- **Refresh concurrency guard** (Phase 7.2 note): if multiple tRPC queries 401 simultaneously, we may fire duplicate silent-refresh windows. Accepted for first-ship — Clerk is idempotent and hidden windows are cheap. Add a single-flight guard if this becomes measurable.
1395	- **Refresh-window timeout tuning**: 30s for silent, 5min for visible. May need adjustment if Clerk's first-time-sign-in flow on slow networks exceeds 30s; monitor after initial rollout.
1396	- **Multi-org switching**: deliberately out of scope. `orgScopedProcedure` usage lands after end-to-end Bearer is proven.
1397	
1398	### Follow-ups from Phase 4 verification
1399	
1400	- **Pending-allowed route gap** (`apps/app/src/proxy.ts`): `isPendingAllowedRoute` originally whitelisted `/account/(.*)` and `/api/trpc/organization.create(.*)` only. New users (pending until first org) hitting `/cli/auth` or `/desktop/auth` were redirected to `/account/welcome`, blocking the token handoff before the `ClientAuthBridge` could render. Added both routes to the matcher. This unblocks first-sign-in token issuance for CLI and desktop; the `/account/welcome` bounce only applies to genuinely-protected surfaces from here on.
1401	- **CDP harness for dev Electron** (`apps/desktop/src/main/bootstrap.ts`): added env-gated `--remote-debugging-port` switch, bound to `127.0.0.1` only, guarded by `!app.isPackaged`. Opt-in via `LIGHTFAST_REMOTE_DEBUG_PORT=<int>`. Verified: port listens, `GET /json/version` responds with WebSocket debugger URL; invalid value warns and skips; unset value is silent. Enables autonomous BrowserWindow drive-through of `/desktop/auth` sign-in during Phase 5+ verification.
1402	- **`webRequest.onBeforeRequest` does NOT accept custom URL schemes** (`apps/desktop/src/main/auth-flow.ts`, spike worktree was wrong): attempting `partition.webRequest.onBeforeRequest({ urls: ["lightfast://*/*"] }, ...)` throws `TypeError: Invalid url pattern lightfast://*/*: Wrong scheme type.` on Electron 33.4.11. Chrome-extension match patterns only allow `http`, `https`, `file`, `ftp`, `urn`. Replaced with `partition.protocol.handle(CALLBACK_SCHEME, handler)` — the supported API for intercepting custom schemes at the network layer. Returns a 204 response; the `will-navigate` channel remains the primary intercept path (fires for JS-driven `window.location = "lightfast://..."`); `protocol.handle` is the safety net for programmatic edge cases. Registration is scoped per-sign-in and `unhandle`d in `settle()`. **Verified via CDP** (14/14 checks): bridge shape, `auth.signIn()` opens BrowserWindow at `/desktop/auth?state=<32-byte hex>`, `persist:lightfast-auth` partition created on disk, cancellation returns `null`, `signOut()` is a safe no-op when signed out.
1403

```
43	  const classes = document.documentElement.classList;
44	  classes.toggle("electron-dark", variant === "dark");
45	  classes.toggle("electron-light", variant === "light");
46	}

48	void window.lightfastBridge.getSystemThemeVariant().then(applyThemeVariant);
49	window.lightfastBridge.onSystemThemeVariantUpdated(applyThemeVariant);

52	if (buildBadge) {

54	}
55	
56	for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("[data-kbd-hint]")) {
57	  const name = el.dataset.kbdHint as AcceleratorName | undefined;
58	  if (name && name in ACCELERATORS) {
59	    el.textContent = formatAccelerator(ACCELERATORS[name], formatPlatform);
60	  }
61	}

63	const sidebar = createSidebarController();

65	
66	function renderForRoute(route: Route): void {
67	  if (route === "settings") {
68	    const root = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("[data-route-settings]");
69	    if (root && root.dataset.rendered !== "true") {
70	      renderSettings(root, formatPlatform);
71	      root.dataset.rendered = "true";
72	    }
73	  }
74	  const items = document.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>(".sidebar .item");
75	  for (const item of items) {
76	    const target = item.dataset.routeTo as Route | undefined;
77	    if (!target) {
78	      continue;
79	    }
80	    item.classList.toggle("active", target === route);
81	  }
82	}
83	
84	renderForRoute(router.current());
85	router.onChange(renderForRoute);
86

92	    if (target) {

111	)) {

113	}
114	
115	function dispatchAction(name: AcceleratorName): void {
116	  switch (name) {
117	    case "toggleSidebar":
118	      sidebar.toggle();
119	      break;
120	    case "settings":
121	      router.navigate("settings");
122	      break;
123	    case "newThread":

125	      break;
126	    case "newWindow":

128	      break;
129	    default:
130	      break;
131	  }
132	}
133	
134	const hotkeys = createHotkeyManager({ platform: formatPlatform });
135	for (const name of Object.keys(ACCELERATORS) as AcceleratorName[]) {
136	  hotkeys.on(name, () => dispatchAction(name));
137	}
138	
139	window.lightfastBridge.onMenuAction((name) => dispatchAction(name));
```

```
1	"use client";
2	
3	import type { AppRouter } from "@api/app";
4	import type { QueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
5	import { MutationCache, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
6	import {
7	  createTRPCClient,
8	  httpBatchStreamLink,
9	  loggerLink,
10	  TRPCClientError,
11	} from "@trpc/client";
12	import { createTRPCContext } from "@trpc/tanstack-react-query";
13	import { useState } from "react";
14	import { toast } from "sonner";
15	import SuperJSON from "superjson";
16	import { createQueryClient } from "./client";
17	
18	export interface CreateTRPCReactProviderOptions {
19	  baseUrl?: string;
20	  getAuthHeaders?: () =>
21	    | Record<string, string>
22	    | Promise<Record<string, string>>;
23	}
24	
25	const trpcContext = createTRPCContext<AppRouter>();
26	
27	export const useTRPC = trpcContext.useTRPC;
28	export const TRPCProvider = trpcContext.TRPCProvider;
29	
30	const mutationCache = new MutationCache({
31	  onError: (error, _variables, _context, mutation) => {
32	    if (mutation.options.meta?.suppressErrorToast) {
33	      return;
34	    }
35	
36	    const title = mutation.options.meta?.errorTitle ?? "Something went wrong";
37	
38	    let message = "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again.";
39	    if (
40	      error instanceof TRPCClientError &&
41	      error.data?.httpStatus != null &&
42	      error.data.httpStatus < 500
43	    ) {
44	      message = error.message;
45	    }
46	
47	    toast.error(title, { description: message });
48	  },
49	});
50	
51	let clientQueryClientSingleton: QueryClient | undefined;
52	
53	function getQueryClient() {
54	  if (typeof window === "undefined") {
55	    return createQueryClient();
56	  }
57	
58	  return (clientQueryClientSingleton ??= createQueryClient({ mutationCache }));
59	}
60	
61	function defaultGetBaseUrl() {
62	  if (typeof window !== "undefined") {
63	    return window.location.origin;
64	  }
65	  if (process.env.VERCEL_URL) {
66	    return `https://${process.env.VERCEL_URL}`;
67	  }
68	  return `http://localhost:${process.env.PORT ?? 4104}`;
69	}
70	
71	export function TRPCReactProvider({
72	  children,
73	  options,
74	}: {
75	  children: React.ReactNode;
76	  options?: CreateTRPCReactProviderOptions;
77	}) {
78	  const queryClient = getQueryClient();
79	
80	  const [trpcClient] = useState(() => {
81	    const baseUrl = options?.baseUrl ?? defaultGetBaseUrl();
82	
83	    return createTRPCClient<AppRouter>({
84	      links: [
85	        loggerLink({
86	          enabled: (op) =>
87	            process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" ||
88	            (op.direction === "down" && op.result instanceof Error),
89	        }),
90	        httpBatchStreamLink({
91	          transformer: SuperJSON,
92	          url: `${baseUrl}/api/trpc`,
93	          headers: async () => ({
94	            "x-trpc-source": "client",
95	            ...((await options?.getAuthHeaders?.()) ?? {}),
96	          }),
97	          fetch(url, init) {
98	            const sameOrigin =
99	              typeof window !== "undefined" &&
100	              new URL(url.toString(), window.location.origin).origin ===
101	                window.location.origin;
102	            return fetch(url, {
103	              ...init,
104	              credentials: sameOrigin ? "include" : "omit",
105	            } as RequestInit);
106	          },
107	        }),
108	      ],
109	    });
110	  });
111	
112	  return (
113	    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
114	      <TRPCProvider queryClient={queryClient} trpcClient={trpcClient}>
115	        {children}
116	      </TRPCProvider>
117	    </QueryClientProvider>
118	  );
119	}
120
```

```
1395	- **Refresh-window timeout tuning**: 30s for silent, 5min for visible. May need adjustment if Clerk's first-time-sign-in flow on slow networks exceeds 30s; monitor after initial rollout.
1396	- **Multi-org switching**: deliberately out of scope. `orgScopedProcedure` usage lands after end-to-end Bearer is proven.
1397	
1398	### Follow-ups from Phase 4 verification
1399	
1400	- **Pending-allowed route gap** (`apps/app/src/proxy.ts`): `isPendingAllowedRoute` originally whitelisted `/account/(.*)` and `/api/trpc/organization.create(.*)` only. New users (pending until first org) hitting `/cli/auth` or `/desktop/auth` were redirected to `/account/welcome`, blocking the token handoff before the `ClientAuthBridge` could render. Added both routes to the matcher. This unblocks first-sign-in token issuance for CLI and desktop; the `/account/welcome` bounce only applies to genuinely-protected surfaces from here on.
1401	- **CDP harness for dev Electron** (`apps/desktop/src/main/bootstrap.ts`): added env-gated `--remote-debugging-port` switch, bound to `127.0.0.1` only, guarded by `!app.isPackaged`. Opt-in via `LIGHTFAST_REMOTE_DEBUG_PORT=<int>`. Verified: port listens, `GET /json/version` responds with WebSocket debugger URL; invalid value warns and skips; unset value is silent. Enables autonomous BrowserWindow drive-through of `/desktop/auth` sign-in during Phase 5+ verification.
1402	- **`webRequest.onBeforeRequest` does NOT accept custom URL schemes** (`apps/desktop/src/main/auth-flow.ts`, spike worktree was wrong): attempting `partition.webRequest.onBeforeRequest({ urls: ["lightfast://*/*"] }, ...)` throws `TypeError: Invalid url pattern lightfast://*/*: Wrong scheme type.` on Electron 33.4.11. Chrome-extension match patterns only allow `http`, `https`, `file`, `ftp`, `urn`. Replaced with `partition.protocol.handle(CALLBACK_SCHEME, handler)` — the supported API for intercepting custom schemes at the network layer. Returns a 204 response; the `will-navigate` channel remains the primary intercept path (fires for JS-driven `window.location = "lightfast://..."`); `protocol.handle` is the safety net for programmatic edge cases. Registration is scoped per-sign-in and `unhandle`d in `settle()`. **Verified via CDP** (14/14 checks): bridge shape, `auth.signIn()` opens BrowserWindow at `/desktop/auth?state=<32-byte hex>`, `persist:lightfast-auth` partition created on disk, cancellation returns `null`, `signOut()` is a safe no-op when signed out.
```

1	# @lightfast/desktop
2	
3	Lightfast desktop app (Electron). Native-looking macOS sidebar via
4	`NSVisualEffectView`, Mica on Windows 11, signed + notarized releases.
5	
6	## Run
7	
8	```bash
9	pnpm -F @lightfast/desktop dev
10	```
11	
12	## The recipe
13	
14	Main process (`src/main/index.ts`):
15	
16	- `vibrancy: "menu"` — macOS `NSVisualEffectView` material
17	- `visualEffectState: "active"` — stay vibrant when unfocused
18	- `titleBarStyle: "hiddenInset"` + `trafficLightPosition: { x: 16, y: 16 }`
19	- `backgroundMaterial: "mica"` — Windows 11 equivalent
20	- `backgroundColor: "#00000000"` — don't paint an opaque background
21	
22	Renderer (`src/renderer/src/styles.css`):
23	
24	- `html, body, #app { background: transparent; }`
25	- Sidebar container: `background: transparent;`
26	- `.titlebar-drag { -webkit-app-region: drag; }` on the top strip;
27	  `-webkit-app-region: no-drag` on buttons.
28	
29	## Release
30	
31	Releases are cut by pushing a tag matching `desktop-v<version>`:
32	
33	```bash
34	git tag desktop-v0.1.0
35	git push origin desktop-v0.1.0
36	```
37	
38	The `Release desktop` workflow then:
39	
40	1. Creates a draft GitHub Release for the tag.
41	2. Builds signed+notarized ZIP and DMG artifacts for both `arm64` and `x64`
42	   via `electron-forge publish` on `macos-14`.
43	3. Generates `latest-mac-<arch>.json` (Squirrel.Mac feed format) and uploads
44	   them to the release. The app's updater points at
45	   `releases/latest/download/latest-mac-${arch}.json`.
46	4. Undrafts the release.
47	
48	### Required GitHub secrets
49	
50	| Secret | Contents |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | e.g. `Developer ID Application: Lightfast, Inc. (TEAMID)` |
53	| `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | Apple Developer Team ID |
54	| `APPLE_CERT_BASE64` | `base64 -i cert.p12 \| pbcopy` of the Developer ID `.p12` |
55	| `APPLE_CERT_PASSWORD` | Password used to export the `.p12` |
56	| `KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD` | Any string — used for the ephemeral CI keychain |
57	| `APPLE_API_KEY_CONTENT` | Full contents of the App Store Connect `.p8` file |
58	| `APPLE_API_KEY_ID` | 10-char key ID for the above `.p8` |
59	| `APPLE_API_ISSUER` | App Store Connect issuer UUID |
60	
61	`GITHUB_TOKEN` is provided automatically — no secret needed.
62	
63	### Local dry-run
64	
65	Run the packager locally without publishing:
66	
67	```bash
68	pnpm -F @lightfast/desktop exec electron-forge package \
69	  --arch=arm64 --platform=darwin
70	```
71	
72	Full sign/notarize/publish locally (requires the same env vars the workflow
73	sets):
74	
75	```bash
76	APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY=... APPLE_TEAM_ID=... \
77	APPLE_API_KEY=$HOME/.private_keys/AuthKey_XXX.p8 \
78	APPLE_API_KEY_ID=... APPLE_API_ISSUER=... \
79	LIGHTFAST_DESKTOP_RELEASE_REPO=lightfastai/lightfast \
80	GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
81	pnpm -F @lightfast/desktop exec electron-forge publish \
82	  --arch=arm64 --platform=darwin
83	```
84	
```

```json
  "new_string": "## Run\n\n```bash\npnpm -F @lightfast/desktop dev\n```\n\n## Local development\n\nThe desktop app is a Clerk-authenticated tRPC client for the `apps/app` API.\nSigned-in requests go through the microfrontends proxy at\n`http://localhost:3024`, not directly to `apps/app` (4107) — the tRPC route's\nCORS only whitelists the 3024 origin in dev.\n\n### Required env var\n\nCreate `apps/desktop/.env.development` (gitignored):\n\n```\nVITE_LIGHTFAST_API_URL=http://localhost:3024\n```\n\nVite injects this into the renderer as `import.meta.env.VITE_LIGHTFAST_API_URL`\nand `DesktopTRPCProvider` uses it to build the tRPC client.\n\n### Clerk JWT template (one-time, per Clerk environment)\n\nIn the Clerk Dashboard, create a JWT template named exactly `lightfast-desktop`:\n\n- **Name**: `lightfast-desktop`\n- **Expiry**: `3600` seconds (1 hour)\n- **Claims**: include `org_id: {{org.id}}` so `orgRouter` procedures work\n- **Signing**: default (symmetric — the server verifies via `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`)\n\nThis must be done once in each Clerk environment (dev and prod). The web\nbridge page (`apps/app/src/app/(auth)/desktop/auth/page.tsx`) calls\n`getToken({ template: \"lightfast-desktop\" })` — without the template,\nsign-in will fail with a 400 from Clerk.\n\n### Run the stack (two terminals)\n\n```bash\n# Terminal 1 — app + www + platform + microfrontends proxy at 3024\npnpm dev:desktop-stack\n\n# Terminal 2 — Electron app\npnpm dev:desktop\n```\n\n`pnpm dev:full` alone is **not** sufficient — it only boots the Next.js apps\nat 4107/4101/4112. The microfrontends proxy at 3024 is a separate process\nlaunched by `dev:desktop-stack` via `concurrently`.\n\n### Inspect the encrypted token store\n\nThe main process persists the Clerk JWT + refresh cookie via `safeStorage`\ninto a keychain-backed file:\n\n```bash\n# macOS\nls ~/Library/Application\\ Support/Lightfast/auth.bin\n```\n\nDelete this file to force a fresh sign-in.\n\n## The recipe"
```

```
1398	### Follow-ups from Phase 4 verification
1399	
1400	- **Pending-allowed route gap** (`apps/app/src/proxy.ts`): `isPendingAllowedRoute` originally whitelisted `/account/(.*)` and `/api/trpc/organization.create(.*)` only. New users (pending until first org) hitting `/cli/auth` or `/desktop/auth` were redirected to `/account/welcome`, blocking the token handoff before the `ClientAuthBridge` could render. Added both routes to the matcher. This unblocks first-sign-in token issuance for CLI and desktop; the `/account/welcome` bounce only applies to genuinely-protected surfaces from here on.
1401	- **CDP harness for dev Electron** (`apps/desktop/src/main/bootstrap.ts`): added env-gated `--remote-debugging-port` switch, bound to `127.0.0.1` only, guarded by `!app.isPackaged`. Opt-in via `LIGHTFAST_REMOTE_DEBUG_PORT=<int>`. Verified: port listens, `GET /json/version` responds with WebSocket debugger URL; invalid value warns and skips; unset value is silent. Enables autonomous BrowserWindow drive-through of `/desktop/auth` sign-in during Phase 5+ verification.
1402	- **`webRequest.onBeforeRequest` does NOT accept custom URL schemes** (`apps/desktop/src/main/auth-flow.ts`, spike worktree was wrong): attempting `partition.webRequest.onBeforeRequest({ urls: ["lightfast://*/*"] }, ...)` throws `TypeError: Invalid url pattern lightfast://*/*: Wrong scheme type.` on Electron 33.4.11. Chrome-extension match patterns only allow `http`, `https`, `file`, `ftp`, `urn`. Replaced with `partition.protocol.handle(CALLBACK_SCHEME, handler)` — the supported API for intercepting custom schemes at the network layer. Returns a 204 response; the `will-navigate` channel remains the primary intercept path (fires for JS-driven `window.location = "lightfast://..."`); `protocol.handle` is the safety net for programmatic edge cases. Registration is scoped per-sign-in and `unhandle`d in `settle()`. **Verified via CDP** (14/14 checks): bridge shape, `auth.signIn()` opens BrowserWindow at `/desktop/auth?state=<32-byte hex>`, `persist:lightfast-auth` partition created on disk, cancellation returns `null`, `signOut()` is a safe no-op when signed out.
1403	
1404	### Follow-ups from Phase 5 verification
1405	
1406	- **pnpm-nested CJS peer resolution for Vite renderer** (`apps/desktop/vite.renderer.config.ts`): Vite's esbuild dep optimizer failed to resolve `copy-anything` (superjson's peer) and `is-what` (copy-anything's peer) when the superjson module was imported through the `@repo/app-trpc` workspace symlink chain — despite `resolve.preserveSymlinks: false` being the default. Root cause: when a workspace package's `node_modules` path contains pnpm-symlinked deps, esbuild's walk found the symlink path rather than the real `.pnpm/<pkg>/node_modules/` store folder where peers are siblings. Fixed with two layers: (a) added `@tanstack/query-core`, `scheduler`, `copy-anything` as explicit `@lightfast/desktop` deps so they're hoisted to `apps/desktop/node_modules` and resolvable without walking through the symlink chain; (b) `optimizeDeps.include: ["@repo/app-trpc/desktop", "@repo/app-trpc/react", "superjson", "sonner"]` in `vite.renderer.config.ts` forces Vite to pre-bundle the workspace entry points from the desktop's resolution context.
1407	- **Module augmentation in shared tRPC package** (`packages/app-trpc/src/react.tsx`): the `Register` augmentation for TanStack Query's `mutationMeta` lives in `packages/app-trpc/src/types.ts`, but nothing in the `./react` or `./desktop` import chain pulls it in. This made `meta?.errorTitle` type out as `{}` from the desktop's tsconfig (passing from app-trpc's own tsconfig, which includes all sources). Added `import "./types";` side-effect import at the top of `react.tsx` so the augmentation travels with any consumer of the react entry.
1408	- **Loose global declaration conflict** (`packages/app-trpc/src/desktop.tsx`): originally declared `window.lightfastBridge?: {...}` with optional chaining. When merged with the desktop's stricter `declare global { interface Window { lightfastBridge: LightfastBridge } }`, TS rejected both with "All declarations of 'lightfastBridge' must have identical modifiers." Removed the global declaration from the shared package entirely; the provider now casts `window` locally to a minimal interface (`{ lightfastBridge?: { auth?: { getToken?: ... } } }`) — the shared package shouldn't be polluting global types it doesn't own. **CDP-verified via 11/11 checks**: React mounts under `#react-root`, Sign In button renders when signed-out, vanilla sidebar/settings DOM still rendered alongside, `window.lightfastBridge` remains exposed and `snapshot.isSignedIn === false`.
```

```
18	function BridgeContent(props: ClientAuthBridgeProps) {

47	  }, [isLoaded, isSignedIn, getToken, props, searchParams]);

62	  return (

66	          {status === "redirecting" ? "Opening Lightfast…" : props.title}
67	        </h1>
```

```
1	import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
2	import { BrowserWindow, session } from "electron";
3	import { setToken } from "./auth-store";
4	
5	const CALLBACK_SCHEME = "lightfast";
6	const PARTITION = "persist:lightfast-auth";
7	const SIGNIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60_000;
8	const REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
9	
10	function getApiOrigin(): string {
11	  return (
12	    process.env.LIGHTFAST_API_URL ??
13	    (process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"
14	      ? "https://lightfast.ai"
15	      : "http://localhost:3024")
16	  );
17	}
18	
19	export interface CallbackResult {
20	  token: string;
21	  state: string;
22	}
23	
24	export function parseCallback(url: string): CallbackResult | null {
25	  try {
26	    const parsed = new URL(url);
27	    if (parsed.protocol !== `${CALLBACK_SCHEME}:`) return null;
28	    if (parsed.host !== "auth") return null;
29	    if (parsed.pathname !== "/callback") return null;
30	    const token = parsed.searchParams.get("token");
31	    const state = parsed.searchParams.get("state");
32	    if (!token || !state) return null;
33	    return { token, state };
34	  } catch {
35	    return null;
36	  }
37	}
38	
39	async function runAuthWindow(options: {
40	  visible: boolean;
41	  timeoutMs: number;
42	}): Promise<string | null> {
43	  const state = randomBytes(32).toString("hex");
44	  const partition = session.fromPartition(PARTITION);
45	  const win = new BrowserWindow({
46	    show: options.visible,
47	    width: 480,
48	    height: 720,
49	    webPreferences: {
50	      session: partition,
51	      contextIsolation: true,
52	      nodeIntegration: false,
53	    },
54	  });
55	
56	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
57	    let settled = false;
58	    let schemeHandled = false;
59	
60	    const settle = (result: CallbackResult | null) => {
61	      if (settled) return;
62	      settled = true;
63	      clearTimeout(timer);
64	      if (schemeHandled) {
65	        try {
66	          partition.protocol.unhandle(CALLBACK_SCHEME);
67	        } catch {
68	          // ignore — unhandle throws if nothing registered
69	        }
70	        schemeHandled = false;
71	      }
72	      if (!win.isDestroyed()) win.close();
73	      if (result && result.state === state) {
74	        setToken(result.token);
75	        resolve(result.token);
76	      } else {
77	        resolve(null);
78	      }
79	    };
80	
81	    const timer = setTimeout(() => settle(null), options.timeoutMs);
82	
83	    // Primary channel: will-navigate fires for JS-driven window.location assignments.
84	    win.webContents.on("will-navigate", (event, url) => {
85	      if (!url.startsWith(`${CALLBACK_SCHEME}://`)) return;
86	      event.preventDefault();
87	      settle(parseCallback(url));
88	    });
89	
90	    // Safety net: if will-navigate somehow doesn't fire (programmatic edge cases,
91	    // meta-refresh redirects), register a custom-scheme handler so the navigation
92	    // reaches us at the network layer. webRequest.onBeforeRequest does NOT accept
93	    // custom schemes in Electron, so protocol.handle is the only supported option.
94	    try {
95	      partition.protocol.handle(CALLBACK_SCHEME, (request) => {
96	        settle(parseCallback(request.url));
97	        return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
98	      });
99	      schemeHandled = true;
100	    } catch (error) {
101	      console.warn(`[auth-flow] protocol.handle(${CALLBACK_SCHEME}) failed`, error);
102	    }
103	
104	    win.on("closed", () => settle(null));
105	
106	    void win.loadURL(
107	      `${getApiOrigin()}/desktop/auth?state=${encodeURIComponent(state)}`
108	    );
109	  });
110	}
111	
112	export async function beginSignIn(): Promise<string | null> {
113	  return runAuthWindow({ visible: true, timeoutMs: SIGNIN_TIMEOUT_MS });
114	}
115	
116	export async function silentRefresh(): Promise<string | null> {
117	  return runAuthWindow({ visible: false, timeoutMs: REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS });
118	}
119
```

Found symptom #2's likely root cause on line 82:

```ts
url.searchParams.set("redirect_url", req.nextUrl.href);
```

`req.nextUrl.href` evaluates to the **internal** origin (4107) when hit through the microfrontends proxy at 3024, not the external origin the BrowserWindow actually loaded. So the flow is:

1. Main process opens BrowserWindow at `http://localhost:3024/desktop/auth?state=<hex>` 
2. Middleware redirects to `http://localhost:3024/sign-in?redirect_url=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A4107%2Fdesktop%2Fauth%3Fstate%3D<hex>`
3. User signs in — Clerk bounces to the `redirect_url`, which is `http://localhost:4107/desktop/auth?state=<hex>`
4. BrowserWindow is now at `4107`, different origin. Clerk's frontend scripts may or may not see the session there (depends on cookie domain + Clerk dev instance config)
5. Bridge component either sees `isSignedIn=false` forever (stuck loading) OR `getToken({ template: "lightfast-desktop" })` returns null because the template isn't set up → should show "Authentication Failed" per `client-auth-bridge.tsx:33-34`

Let me not rush into patches. Here's what I found and where I think we should pause to align:

## What I actually found (vs. what I reported)

**My testing gap, plainly:** I ran typechecks (pass) and a single curl probe (`/desktop/auth?state=test` → 307 → 200) and called Phase 6 green. I never completed a real sign-in. That's on me — the flow has at least one real bug I missed.

## The bug in the redirect_url

`apps/app/src/proxy.ts:82`:
```ts
url.searchParams.set("redirect_url", req.nextUrl.href);
```

`req.nextUrl.href` is the **internal** URL after the microfrontends proxy forwards it — always `http://localhost:4107/...`, never the `3024` origin the BrowserWindow actually loaded. So:

- Main process opens BrowserWindow at `http://localhost:3024/desktop/auth?state=<hex>` ✓
- Middleware sends `→ /sign-in?redirect_url=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A4107%2Fdesktop%2Fauth%3Fstate%3D<hex>` ✗
- User signs in at `3024/sign-in`, Clerk bounces to `4107/desktop/auth?state=<hex>` — cross-origin from where the window started
- On `4107`, Clerk frontend's session handling may fail (cookie scope, CORS, or Clerk dev instance domain binding) → `useAuth()` stays `isSignedIn=false` → effect in `client-auth-bridge.tsx:25-47` never fires → stuck on "Authenticating…"

Same bug exists for `/cli/auth` — it just hasn't surfaced because CLI flow hits `apps/app` directly, not through the proxy.

## The design question: Electron window vs OS browser

Phase 4's spike explicitly chose Electron `BrowserWindow` over `shell.openExternal`, with this reasoning (plan line 1371):
> Replaced `shell.openExternal` with `BrowserWindow`-based sign-in (Phase 4.2). Added Phase 7 for silent refresh. Removed hourly re-auth UX burden — users now re-auth only when their Clerk session itself expires (days).

The spike concluded that OS-browser + `lightfast://` deeplink back is flaky on macOS (new instance spawn, credential handoff loss). The Electron window gets a persistent `persist:lightfast-auth` session that silently re-mints JWTs forever (Phase 7).

**Your statement "it should actually open the browser" contradicts this choice.** Before I start patching, I need to know which of these you mean:

1. **You want OS browser instead of Electron window.** Big reversal — unwinds the Phase 4 spike, the persistent partition, and Phase 7's silent refresh. Real credential-handoff problems the spike already identified return. Probably 2-3 days of rework.
2. **Electron window is fine, you were just describing the broken-ness.** Then the real fix is: (a) redirect_url bug, (b) JWT template setup, (c) a visible error state when `getToken` returns null so users don't sit on a silent spinner.
3. **Something else** — like "I expected it to open the signed-in web app in the real browser when authed". In that case we're talking about a different feature entirely (e.g. a "Open in browser" button on the signed-in shell).

Which is it? I don't want to guess and then have to unwind more work.

For what it's worth, my recommendation is **(2)** — the bug is real and fixable (an hour of work), the Phase 4 spike's reasoning still holds, and Phase 6's "JWT template is a prereq" step is real but currently silent on failure. But your call.

Noted. A few things to align on before I start cutting code — this unwinds more than just the BrowserWindow:

**Recommended approach: loopback HTTP server (RFC 8252 native-app pattern)**
1. Main process starts an ephemeral HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:<random-port>` with a `/callback` route
2. Click sign-in → `shell.openExternal('http://localhost:3024/desktop/auth?state=<hex>&callback=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback')`
3. User signs in (fast path if already signed in to lightfast.ai in that browser)
4. Bridge page gets token from Clerk, redirects the tab to the loopback callback URL with `?token=…&state=…`
5. Loopback server receives, saves token, responds with a "You can close this tab" HTML, shuts down
6. IPC flips the renderer to signed-in

This is what `gcloud auth`, GitHub CLI, etc. use. More reliable than `lightfast://` deeplinks (no OS protocol registration, no macOS "new instance spawn" issue, no "credential handoff" concern — token is in the URL).

**The tradeoff you're accepting:**
- **Phase 7 silent refresh is gone.** The whole reason for the `persist:lightfast-auth` BrowserWindow partition was to re-mint JWTs using the cookie we already had. With OS browser, we don't own that cookie.
- Fix: make the `lightfast-desktop` JWT template longer-lived (24h–7d) so users re-sign-in occasionally. Or add a proper Clerk refresh-token exchange (more code, another day of work).

**On `/cli/auth` being old code:** confirmed — happy to leave it untouched (delete later). Means only `/desktop/auth` needs touching for this reversal. The shared `ClientAuthBridge` becomes desktop-only in practice.

**Scope of rip-out:**
- `apps/desktop/src/main/auth-flow.ts` — replace BrowserWindow with `shell.openExternal` + loopback server
- `apps/desktop/src/main/protocol.ts` — simplify (no `lightfast://` interception needed)
- `apps/app/.../desktop-auth-client.tsx` — read `callback` from query, redirect there instead of `lightfast://`
- `apps/app/src/proxy.ts:82` — fix `redirect_url` bug (still needed — user lands on `/sign-in` if signed out)
- Delete Phase 7 plan + `persist:lightfast-auth` partition references
- Revise README

Want me to go ahead with loopback, or do you prefer deeplink (`lightfast://`) with `shell.openExternal` and a `second-instance` handler? Loopback is cleaner but one more moving part (the tiny HTTP server); deeplink is less code but needs OS protocol registration to actually work per-platform.

> AGENT

Short explanation:

**Deeplink (`lightfast://...`)** — a custom URL scheme registered with the OS. When the browser opens `lightfast://auth/callback?token=xxx`, the OS hands that URL off to our Electron app. Think of it like `mailto:` → opens your email app.

**Loopback** — our Electron app starts a tiny HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:54321` (random port). The browser redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:54321/callback?token=xxx` which talks HTTP to our local server.

## Which is best for you

**Loopback wins for this project.** Recommendation, not a close call:

| | Deeplink | Loopback |
|---|---|---|
| OS registration | Yes, per platform | None |
| Platform-specific code | `open-url` (macOS), `second-instance` (Win/Linux) | Zero — just Node `http` |
| "App already running" edge cases | Need `requestSingleInstanceLock` + handler plumbing | None — browser talks to already-running server |
| macOS dev pain | Stale protocol associations, packaging setup | None |
| Used by | Slack, Linear, 1Password | gcloud, GitHub CLI, AWS CLI |
| Code size | ~60 lines but across 3 files | ~80 lines in one place |

The one thing deeplink gives you: no firewall anything. But `127.0.0.1` loopback doesn't trigger macOS/Windows firewall prompts either — it's not a listening-on-network socket.

The only real reason to pick deeplink is "it feels more native" (the browser flashes your app's name when redirecting). For a dev tool, that's not worth the platform glue.

**My call: loopback.** Want me to proceed?

```json
  "content": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { ClientAuthBridge } from \"../../../_components/client-auth-bridge\";\n\nconst LOOPBACK_HOSTS = new Set([\"127.0.0.1\", \"localhost\"]);\n\nfunction validateLoopbackCallback(raw: string | null): URL | null {\n  if (!raw) return null;\n  try {\n    const parsed = new URL(raw);\n    if (parsed.protocol !== \"http:\") return null;\n    if (!LOOPBACK_HOSTS.has(parsed.hostname)) return null;\n    if (parsed.pathname !== \"/callback\") return null;\n    return parsed;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nexport function DesktopAuthClient() {\n  return (\n    <ClientAuthBridge\n      title=\"Authenticating…\"\n      subtitle=\"You'll be redirected back to the Lightfast desktop app shortly.\"\n      jwtTemplate=\"lightfast-desktop\"\n      buildRedirectUrl={({ token, searchParams }) => {\n        const state = searchParams.get(\"state\");\n        const callback = validateLoopbackCallback(searchParams.get(\"callback\"));\n        if (!state || !callback) return null;\n        callback.searchParams.set(\"token\", token);\n        callback.searchParams.set(\"state\", state);\n        return callback.toString();\n      }}\n    />\n  );\n}\n"
}
```
