1	# @lightfast/desktop
2	
3	Lightfast desktop app (Electron). Native-looking macOS sidebar via
4	`NSVisualEffectView`, Mica on Windows 11, signed + notarized releases.
5	
6	## Run
7	
8	```bash
9	pnpm -F @lightfast/desktop dev
10	```
11	
12	## Local development
13	
14	The desktop app is a Clerk-authenticated tRPC client for the `apps/app` API.
15	Signed-in requests go through the microfrontends proxy at
16	`http://localhost:3024`, not directly to `apps/app` (4107) — the tRPC route's
17	CORS only whitelists the 3024 origin in dev.
18	
19	### Required env var
20	
21	Create `apps/desktop/.env.development` (gitignored):
22	
23	```
24	VITE_LIGHTFAST_API_URL=http://localhost:3024
25	```
26	
27	Vite injects this into the renderer as `import.meta.env.VITE_LIGHTFAST_API_URL`
28	and `DesktopTRPCProvider` uses it to build the tRPC client.
29	
30	### Clerk JWT template (one-time, per Clerk environment)
31	
32	In the Clerk Dashboard, create a JWT template named exactly `lightfast-desktop`:
33	
34	- **Name**: `lightfast-desktop`
35	- **Expiry**: `3600` seconds (1 hour)
36	- **Claims**: include `org_id: {{org.id}}` so `orgRouter` procedures work
37	- **Signing**: default (symmetric — the server verifies via `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`)
38	
39	This must be done once in each Clerk environment (dev and prod). The web
40	bridge page (`apps/app/src/app/(auth)/desktop/auth/page.tsx`) calls
41	`getToken({ template: "lightfast-desktop" })` — without the template,
42	sign-in will fail with a 400 from Clerk.
43	
44	### Run the stack (two terminals)
45	
46	```bash
47	# Terminal 1 — app + www + platform + microfrontends proxy at 3024
48	pnpm dev:desktop-stack
49	
50	# Terminal 2 — Electron app
51	pnpm dev:desktop
52	```
53	
54	`pnpm dev:full` alone is **not** sufficient — it only boots the Next.js apps
55	at 4107/4101/4112. The microfrontends proxy at 3024 is a separate process
56	launched by `dev:desktop-stack` via `concurrently`.
57	
58	### Inspect the encrypted token store
59	
60	The main process persists the Clerk JWT + refresh cookie via `safeStorage`
61	into a keychain-backed file:
62	
63	```bash
64	# macOS
65	ls ~/Library/Application\ Support/Lightfast/auth.bin
66	```
67	
68	Delete this file to force a fresh sign-in.
69	
70	## The recipe
71	
72	Main process (`src/main/index.ts`):
73	
74	- `vibrancy: "menu"` — macOS `NSVisualEffectView` material
75	- `visualEffectState: "active"` — stay vibrant when unfocused
76	- `titleBarStyle: "hiddenInset"` + `trafficLightPosition: { x: 16, y: 16 }`
77	- `backgroundMaterial: "mica"` — Windows 11 equivalent
78	- `backgroundColor: "#00000000"` — don't paint an opaque background
79	
80	Renderer (`src/renderer/src/styles.css`):
```

The bridge page calls `getToken({ template: \"lightfast-desktop\" })` — without it, sign-in fails with a 400 from Clerk and no amount of code changes will paper over it. Readme now explicitly lists this alongside the env var and the two-terminal run procedure, plus an `auth.bin` inspect path for debugging.\n\n### Design reversal: OS browser + loopback callback (2026-04-23)\n\n**Triggering feedback**: manual drive-through surfaced two problems that I had not caught in automated verification. (1) Signed-out BrowserWindow hit `/desktop/auth?state=…` → middleware redirected to `/sign-in?redirect_url=<4107-origin>` because `req.nextUrl.href` reflects the internal microfrontends target, not the 3024 proxy the window actually loaded. (2) Even when signed in, the user preferred to sign in through their real browser rather than an Electron-hosted BrowserWindow. \"It should actually open the browser\" was the explicit ask.\n\n**Decision**: reverse Phase 4's BrowserWindow design in favour of the RFC 8252 \"native app\" pattern — `shell.openExternal` + an ephemeral loopback HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:<random-port>`. Same pattern as `gcloud auth`, `gh auth login`, `aws sso login`. Explicitly considered custom-scheme deeplinks (`lightfast://`) and rejected them: they require per-platform handler plumbing (`open-url` on macOS, `second-instance` on Win/Linux), stale-association dev pain on macOS, and protocol registration at packaging time. Loopback needs only the Node `http` module and works identically on all three platforms.\n\n**Scope of rip-out**:\n\n- **`apps/desktop/src/main/auth-flow.ts`** — full rewrite. Replaced `BrowserWindow` + `partition.protocol.handle(CALLBACK_SCHEME, …)` + `will-navigate` interception with: Node `createServer()` bound to `127.0.0.1:0` (OS assigns port), `shell.openExternal(signInUrl)` where `signInUrl` carries both `state` (nonce) and `callback=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`. The server handles one GET `/callback`, validates `state`, persists the token via `setToken`, responds with a small \"Signed in / close this tab\" HTML page, and `server.close()`s. `SIGNIN_TIMEOUT_MS` still set to 5 minutes. `silentRefresh()`, `parseCallback()`, `CALLBACK_SCHEME`, and `PARTITION` all removed.\n- **`apps/desktop/src/main/protocol.ts`** — **deleted**. The file registered `lightfast://` as the default protocol client, wired `open-url` / `second-instance` handlers, and delivered captured URLs into a `onDeepLink` listener that only did a window focus + `console.log` by the end of Phase 5. With auth migrated off deeplinks, nothing else uses it; the `requestSingleInstanceLock` in `bootstrap.ts` covers single-instance independently.\n- **`apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts`** — removed `registerProtocolHandler()` call, `onDeepLink` listener, and the three `./protocol` imports. No behavioural change beyond what the deletion above implies.\n- **`apps/desktop/forge.config.ts`** — removed `CFBundleURLTypes` entry + `PROTOCOL_SCHEME` constant. The packaged `Info.plist` no longer advertises `lightfast://` handling.\n- **`apps/app/.../desktop-auth-client.tsx`** — `buildRedirectUrl` now reads `callback` (not builds a `lightfast://` URL), validates it strictly via a `validateLoopbackCallback(raw)` helper (allowed: `http:`, hostname ∈ {`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`}, pathname === `/callback`), and appends `token` + `state` as query params. **Security**: this validation is non-negotiable. Without it an attacker-crafted `/desktop/auth?state=X&callback=https://evil.com/steal` would exfiltrate the minted JWT to a third-party. The check mirrors what the main process sends, so legitimate callbacks always match.\n- **`apps/app/src/proxy.ts`** — fixed `redirect_url` bug at line 82 (independent of this reversal but needed for the flow to work). Added `externalHref(req)` helper that prefers `x-forwarded-host` + `x-forwarded-proto`, falls back to `req.headers.get(\"host\")`, falls back to `req.nextUrl.href` as last resort. Dev-only — in prod, trusting `x-forwarded-*` from the Vercel edge is fine because Vercel strips/signs them; the helper explicitly gates on `NODE_ENV !== \"production\"`.\n- **`apps/desktop/README.md`** — replaced \"visible Electron BrowserWindow\" copy with the OS-browser flow, bumped JWT template expiry to 24h (since there's no silent refresh to mask token expiry), documented the callback validation contract.\n\n**Phase 7 is dead.** Silent refresh via hidden BrowserWindow depended on the `persist:lightfast-auth` partition owning Clerk's `__session` cookie. With the OS browser owning that cookie now, we can't re-mint JWTs without another user click. The tradeoff is explicit and accepted: a 24-hour JWT expiry means users re-authenticate once per day, and the renderer's existing 401 handler in `app-shell.tsx` gracefully flips the UI back to the Sign In state when a token expires mid-session. A future enhancement could add Clerk refresh-token exchange for silent re-issuance — but that's a separate design, not Phase 7.\n\n**CLI auth bridge left untouched** per user note (\"cli/auth is old code, most likely wrong\"). The shared `ClientAuthBridge` component remains in `apps/app/src/app/(app)/(user)/(pending-not-allowed)/_components/` — it's still reusable for any future deeplink-based surface, but desktop no longer exercises the `lightfast://` code path.\n\n**What re-verification is still owed (human only):**\n1. Create Clerk JWT template `lightfast-desktop` (24h expiry, `org_id: {{org.id}}` claim).\n2. `pnpm dev:desktop-stack` + `pnpm dev:desktop`.\n3. Click Sign In → default browser opens at `localhost:3024/desktop/auth?state=…&callback=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`.\n4. Complete Clerk sign-in → tab redirects to the loopback URL → sees \"Signed in\" page → can close tab.\n5. Desktop renderer flips to signed-in, `AccountCard` renders user profile, network tab shows `Authorization: Bearer …` headers on `/api/trpc/account.get`.\n6. Negative paths: close browser tab before sign-in (timeout → null), malicious `callback` param (bridge rejects, shows \"Authentication Failed\"), second-process callback attempt (loopback server closed → 404).\n\nI will not call this verified until the user has walked through the golden path."
}

Loopback redesign landed. Summary of changes:

**Main process**
- `apps/desktop/src/main/auth-flow.ts` — full rewrite. Ephemeral Node HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:<random-port>`, `shell.openExternal` to the default browser with `?state=<hex>&callback=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`. Server validates state, persists token, responds with a tiny "Signed in / close this tab" page, then shuts down. `silentRefresh`, `parseCallback`, `CALLBACK_SCHEME`, `PARTITION` all gone.
- `apps/desktop/src/main/protocol.ts` — **deleted** (nothing else consumed deeplinks).
- `apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts` — removed `registerProtocolHandler` + `onDeepLink` wiring.
- `apps/desktop/forge.config.ts` — removed `CFBundleURLTypes` + `PROTOCOL_SCHEME`.

**Web bridge**
- `apps/app/.../desktop-auth-client.tsx` — reads `callback` query param, rejects anything that isn't `http://(127.0.0.1|localhost):<port>/callback`, appends `token`+`state` and redirects. Strict validation is load-bearing — without it, an attacker-crafted `/desktop/auth?callback=https://evil.com` would exfiltrate tokens.
- `apps/app/src/proxy.ts` — added `externalHref(req)` helper that uses `x-forwarded-host`/`x-forwarded-proto` in dev so `redirect_url` points at the 3024 proxy the user actually hit, not the internal 4107.

**Docs / plan**
- `apps/desktop/README.md` — OS-browser flow documented, JWT template expiry bumped to 24h (no silent refresh).
- Plan's Improvement Log gained a "Design reversal: OS browser + loopback callback" section explaining what I unwound from Phase 4 and why Phase 7 is dead.

**Typechecks**: `@lightfast/desktop` + `@lightfast/app` both pass.

2. `pnpm dev:desktop-stack` + `pnpm dev:desktop`.

4. Complete sign-in → tab redirects to `127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` → "Signed in" page, can close tab.
5. Desktop flips to signed-in, AccountCard renders.

If it breaks, tell me where (browser console log, main-process log at `/tmp/desktop-dev.log`, network tab), and I'll actually debug it this time instead of hand-waving.

> AGENT

Found it.

```
▲ Microfrontends Proxy (2.3.2) Started
  - Fallback Applications:
    • lightfast-app → lightfast-app.vercel.app     ← routing to PROD
    • lightfast-www → lightfast-app.vercel.app     ← routing to PROD
```

The proxy started before `apps/app` finished booting on 4107, so it locked in the **fallback** (Vercel prod) for the whole session. That's why your sign-in ran against `lightfast-app.vercel.app`, which rightly rejects the `localhost:3024` origin with production Clerk keys.

Root cause: `dev:desktop-stack` runs `pnpm dev:full` and `pnpm --filter @lightfast/app proxy` concurrently. Turbo's dev cold-start takes ~10s for 3 Next apps + Inngest; the proxy's health check at startup misses 4107, picks fallback, and never recovers.

Let me check what the proxy CLI supports, then fix:

> AGENT

Found it — two issues:

1. **The renderer is hitting `https://lightfast.ai`, not `http://localhost:3024`.** Vite didn't load `.env.development` because its project root is `src/renderer/`, not `apps/desktop/`. So `VITE_LIGHTFAST_API_URL` is undefined at runtime, and `entry.tsx` falls back to `https://lightfast.ai`.
2. CSP then correctly blocks the prod URL (because connect-src doesn't whitelist it).

Fix: tell Vite where to find the env file.

> AGENT

Real issue surfaced — the tRPC URL is now correct (`localhost:3024`), but the CORS **preflight** (OPTIONS) is being redirected by the middleware to `/sign-in` because it has no session cookie. Browsers reject redirects on preflight → `ERR_INVALID_REDIRECT`.

The middleware treats `/api/trpc/(.*)` as a protected route. That's correct for browser cookie auth but breaks Bearer-auth desktop clients because OPTIONS never carries auth. Fix: move `/api/trpc/(.*)` into `isApiRoute` — the tRPC procedures enforce auth themselves via `userScopedProcedure` / `orgScopedProcedure` at the handler level.

> AGENT

Two things are wrong:

1. **Middleware redirects the preflight** because `/api/trpc/(.*)` isn't in `isApiRoute`, so it goes through `auth.protect()` → 307 to `/sign-in`. Preflight can't follow redirects → `ERR_INVALID_REDIRECT`.
2. **CORS doesn't allow `http://localhost:5173`** (the Electron renderer's Vite origin), only `3024` and `wwwUrl`.

Both need fixing.

  "content": "const targets = await (await fetch(\"http://127.0.0.1:9229/json\")).json();\nconst page = targets.find(t => t.type === \"page\" && t.url.includes(\"localhost:5173\"));\nconst ws = new WebSocket(page.webSocketDebuggerUrl);\nawait new Promise((r, e) => { ws.addEventListener(\"open\", () => r()); ws.addEventListener(\"error\", e); });\nlet id = 0; const pending = new Map();\nconst send = (method, params = {}) => {\n  const mid = ++id;\n  return new Promise((r, e) => { pending.set(mid, { resolve: r, reject: e }); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: mid, method, params })); });\n};\n\nconst requestsByReqId = new Map();\nconst failedByReqId = new Map();\nconst responsesByReqId = new Map();\n\nws.addEventListener(\"message\", ev => {\n  const m = JSON.parse(ev.data);\n  if (m.id !== undefined) {\n    const p = pending.get(m.id);\n    if (p) { pending.delete(m.id); m.error ? p.reject(new Error(m.error.message)) : p.resolve(m.result); }\n  } else if (m.method === \"Network.requestWillBeSent\") {\n    const r = m.params.request;\n    if (r.url.includes(\"/api/trpc/\")) {\n      requestsByReqId.set(m.params.requestId, {\n        method: r.method, url: r.url,\n        headers: r.headers,\n      });\n    }\n  } else if (m.method === \"Network.responseReceived\") {\n    if (requestsByReqId.has(m.params.requestId)) {\n      responsesByReqId.set(m.params.requestId, {\n        status: m.params.response.status,\n        headers: m.params.response.headers,\n        mimeType: m.params.response.mimeType,\n      });\n    }\n  } else if (m.method === \"Network.loadingFailed\") {\n    if (requestsByReqId.has(m.params.requestId)) {\n      failedByReqId.set(m.params.requestId, {\n        errorText: m.params.errorText,\n        type: m.params.type,\n        blockedReason: m.params.blockedReason,\n        corsErrorStatus: m.params.corsErrorStatus,\n      });\n    }\n  }\n});\n\nawait send(\"Network.enable\");\nawait send(\"Runtime.enable\");\nawait send(\"Page.enable\");\nawait send(\"Page.reload\", { ignoreCache: true });\nawait new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 4000));\n\nfor (const [rid, req] of requestsByReqId.entries()) {\n  console.log(`\\n=== REQUEST ${rid} ===`);\n  console.log(req.method, req.url.slice(0, 120));\n  console.log(\"  headers:\", Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(req.headers).slice(0, 12)));\n  if (responsesByReqId.has(rid)) {\n    const r = responsesByReqId.get(rid);\n    console.log(`  → response status=${r.status} mime=${r.mimeType}`);\n    const interesting = {};\n    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(r.headers)) {\n      if (/access-control|content-type|x-clerk|location/i.test(k)) interesting[k] = v;\n    }\n    console.log(\"  response headers:\", interesting);\n  }\n  if (failedByReqId.has(rid)) {\n    console.log(\"  → FAILED:\", failedByReqId.get(rid));\n  }\n}\nws.close();\n"

## What the full chain actually proved

1. Click Sign In (Electron) → `shell.openExternal` → OS browser opens `http://localhost:3024/desktop/auth?state=…&callback=http://127.0.0.1:59843/callback`
2. Clerk `/sign-in` handles the `redirect_url` correctly (pointing at **local** 3024, not Vercel prod — that was fix #1)
3. You signed in with your real Clerk dev session
4. Bridge page called `getToken({ template: "lightfast-desktop" })` → returned a real 796-char RS256 JWT with `org_id` claim
5. Bridge page validated the `callback` loopback URL and redirected the browser tab
6. Main-process loopback server received the callback, validated `state`, persisted the token via `safeStorage`, rendered success page
7. Renderer (`AppShell`) flipped from auth-gate to AccountCard
8. AccountCard's tRPC call to `account.get` round-tripped through the middleware (fix #3) + proper CORS (fixes #4/#5) and rendered your real name + email

## The four extra fixes beyond the loopback redesign

1. **`apps/app/src/proxy.ts`** — `externalHref(req)` so `redirect_url` uses the 3024 proxy origin instead of the internal 4107.
2. **`apps/app/package.json`** — proxy script gains `--local-apps lightfast-app lightfast-www` + a `proxy:wait` variant; without these the microfrontends proxy cold-starts into fallback mode and serves your dev app from `lightfast-app.vercel.app` (which has prod Clerk keys locked to `lightfast.ai` — the original "Production Keys" error you saw).
3. **`apps/app/src/proxy.ts`** — added `/api/trpc/(.*)` to `isApiRoute`. The middleware was redirecting CORS preflight OPTIONS to `/sign-in`, which browsers reject with `ERR_INVALID_REDIRECT`. tRPC procedures enforce auth themselves, so this is safe.
4. **`apps/app/src/app/(trpc)/api/trpc/[trpc]/route.ts`** — CORS now allows `http://localhost:5173` (Electron renderer Vite origin) and `trpc-accept` header (used by `httpBatchStreamLink` v11).
5. **`apps/desktop/vite.renderer.config.ts`** — `envDir` pointed at `apps/desktop/` so Vite actually loads `.env.development`. Without this `VITE_LIGHTFAST_API_URL` was undefined and the renderer fell through to `https://lightfast.ai`.

Everything's still running — sign-out round-trip is worth one more poke if you want the full loop. Want me to stop here and commit all of Phase 6 + the loopback redesign + these five fixes, or keep going with the remaining negative-path checks?
